title: Introduction
container-title: Environmental Justice in Digital Worlds
f2f52c38a7a73aa0cb5a9acdafbd209f152f4fe6.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter begins with examples of Mixed Reality technology currently in existence or soon likely to be. These examples motivate a description of what the book is and an argument for why it’s important: that society is on the cusp of widespread technological change which has radical implications for the world, and that it is important to think through what these technologies mean for our environment. It discusses the ways different audiences may engage with this book, and how by using these philosophical tools to look at emerging technologies, this book engages in a process of “technophilosophy” that will examine both the philosophical frameworks and the technologies. The introduction ends with a brief summary of each chapter.</jats:p>

title: Environmental Justice in More-Than-Physical Environments
container-title: Environmental Justice in Digital Worlds
30c810e4e34bf3d572d92380ff471cc35f8b53cf.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter introduces environmental philosophy, and particularly environmental justice, that will be an underlying framework for the book’s approach. The chapter argues that “the environment” ought to include the technologically shaped environments people actually live in, rather than only referring to wild places undamaged by humans. It further argues that environmental philosophy ought to also incorporate virtual entities in material surroundings or even wholly virtual environments. The chapter then introduces a framework for environmental justice, which looks at distributional, participatory, and recognition justice as well as self-determination for individuals and communities when thinking about environmental goods as well as bads, and opportunities as well as risks.</jats:p>

title: Mixing Reality
container-title: Environmental Justice in Digital Worlds
dbb8a9dd5cbe4b161c1a8a14adcfb4674776f777.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter looks in depth at what “Mixed Reality technology” is and which digital technologies will count for the book’s purposes. It defends the critical approach the book takes to looking at technology and the optimism that the roles it plays in society can be democratically shaped, as well as the more pessimistic treadmill path that these developing technologies will take absent just participation in their design and implementation by stakeholders. The chapter also includes a philosophical discussion of the ontological status of the virtual entities that are being mixed into our material world, as well as the partial and fully virtual places we are creating.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Mixed Reality
container-title: Environmental Justice in Digital Worlds
e04323502a4b153b2e9de555a487f931fc1a6812.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>This chapter looks at the ways in which Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Mixed Reality are inextricably linked. To do that, this chapter first looks at what is meant by current “Artificial Intelligence” and argues that in some ways it is best thought of as being neither artificial nor intelligent. The chapter then discusses the various ways in which Mixed Reality is the “eyes and ears” of AI, including using data collected via MR to train AI, using AI to create or improve MR elements in real time, and using AI to process MR data for users to allow a more minimally virtual mixed reality. Ultimately, the chapter argues that AI and MR work in concert to alter our experience of the environment and people’s roles in it.</jats:p>

title: Capacity Limits in Cognitive Processing Reflect the Curse of Generalization
65a5e431acc5d0a8d2c5143f2e9ef4740d73e2de.abstract: The striking constraints of some human cognitive processes stand in stark contrastto the near limitless capability of others. While we can acquire and flexibly use vast amountsof information, the amount we can process at any one time is often stiflingly limited: forexample the number of items we can hold in working memory or the number of tasks that canbe performed at once. Here, we integrate ideas from information theory, cognitive science,and neuroscience to offer a unified account of why processing is often so limited. We arguethat this reflects a fundamental tradeoff between generalization—how effectively existingrepresentations can be used in novel settings—and how many distinct representations canbe processed in parallel. Representations that best promote strong forms of generalization— a characteristically human cognitive strength — come at the expense of surprisinglystrict limits in the number of items that can be processed at once, an equally characteristichuman weakness. We refer to this as the “curse of generalization.” We formulate this first ininformation-theoretic terms, and then in process models, including a neural network modelof classic tasks used to demonstrate strict limits in human processing capacity. This tensionoffers a potential explanation for a range of phenomena — from performance on the tasks onwhich we focus, to representational learning and skill acquisition more broadly — as wellas the performance of modern machine learning architectures that exhibit generalizationcapabilities comparable to humans.

title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
container-title: eLife
42e0bff514a13e990dde6d5376170bcb87804ae4.abstract: <jats:p>The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Effectiveness, Engagement, and Acceptability of a Smartwatch Healthy Lifestyle Intervention for Cognitive Enhancement in Healthy Adults: Mixed Methods Electroencephalography Protocol
container-title: JMIR Research Protocols
7e6b65fd0eceaed8ad891218da9c81d3f193d863.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Wearable technologies are rapidly transforming the health care landscape by enabling the tracking of real-time physiological and behavioral data used in healthy lifestyle interventions. Despite their widespread adoption in the consumer market, scientific validation of their impact on the brain remains limited, and factors influencing effects on cognition and adherence are not fully understood. This gap is critical, as consumers, health care providers, and researchers depend on these data to unlock the potential of wearables for cognitive support.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We aim to assess the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of a commercially available smartwatch healthy lifestyle intervention on cognitive enhancement in healthy adults, using a convergent parallel mixed methods design. We seek to provide a comprehensive, replicable methodological framework to evaluate wearable technology interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Healthy adults aged 18 to 40 years with a sedentary lifestyle (N=72) interested in participating in a healthy lifestyle intervention will be recruited in the Vancouver Metropolitan Area, BC, Canada. Participants will be randomly assigned into an intervention group using an Apple Watch or a control group following standard physical activity guidelines without an Apple Watch for a period of 4 weeks. Effectiveness will be evaluated through (1) cognitive function (primary outcome)—executive function, specifically inhibitory control, via electroencephalogram-based event-related potentials (N2/P3) during a go/no-go task; (2) resting-state brain activity via electroencephalogram spectral power; (3) behavioral performance (reaction time and accuracy); (4) perceived health (36-item Short Form Health Survey); and (5) qualitative analysis of factors affecting the intervention’s effectiveness. Engagement will be assessed through goal completion metrics and qualitative analysis of barriers, facilitators, and usage patterns. Acceptability will be assessed through System Usability Scale scores and qualitative analysis of factors affecting usability, satisfaction, and user preferences. This design integrates assessments before, during, and after intervention. Qualitative assessments will include weekly check-ins and semistructured interviews to obtain a comprehensive understanding of factors influencing the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of the intervention. Exploratory outcomes include descriptions of possible interactions between the 3 constructs and comparison of smartwatch-tracked vs self-reported goal completion.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The study received funding from the AGE-WELL Network Centres of Excellence (April 2020-March 2023) and was approved by the Simon Fraser University Research Ethics Board. Enrollment for the study is ongoing. As of October 2026, data have been collected from 48 participants and are currently being processed and analyzed. The first results are expected to be published in 2027.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This study outlines a foundational framework for evaluating the effectiveness, engagement, and acceptability of wearable health interventions targeting cognitive enhancement in healthy adults. Furthermore, our mixed methods approach with randomized controlled comparison is expected to inform the design and development of effective, engaging, and friendly wearable brain health technologies.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Ambivalencias en torno a las técnicas de reproducción asistida
Ambivalences Regarding Assisted Reproductive Technologies
container-title: Análisis Filosófico
b86ff439826d1f77775ac23357cee21dae26a817.abstract: <jats:p>Este artículo analiza las técnicas de reproducción asistida (TRHA) desde una perspectiva feminista, abordando las tensiones entre autonomía, deseo y justicia. Se examinan las implicancias éticas de la medicalización, la mercantilización del cuerpo, y las normas de género y familia que estas tecnologías pueden reforzar o desafiar. A partir del concepto de autonomía relacional, se considera cómo las condiciones sociales, económicas y culturales influyen en las decisiones reproductivas. Se propone integrar la ética del cuidado y la justicia reproductiva como marcos analíticos que permitan una comprensión más inclusiva y crítica de las TRHA, con énfasis en la equidad, la dignidad y los derechos.</jats:p>

title: Ética y gobernanza de la inteligencia artificial en los procesos educativos de las Fuerzas Militares de Colombia
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
af434ca184d59d5ddf93af8a7cfe27022962cd0f.abstract: <jats:p>Este capítulo presenta un análisis sobre los marcos éticos y de gobernanza para el uso de la inteligencia artificial (IA) en la educación, con especial énfasis en su incorporación en las Fuerzas Militares de Colombia. El objetivo es proponer lineamientos estratégicos que orienten un uso ético, responsable y contextualizado de la IA en los procesos educativos militares. Metodológicamente, se realizó una revisión documental de políticas institucionales nacionales e internacionales, contrastadas con recomendaciones de organismos como la UNESCO y la OCDE, así como diálogos académicos con expertos en la materia. Entre los resultados se identifican buenas prácticas y principios comunes, como la transparencia, la equidad y la alfabetización digital. Las conclusiones destacan la necesidad urgente de establecer políticas adaptadas al entorno militar, promover la formación crítica en IA en todos los niveles y garantizar que esta tecnología habilitadora complemente, mas no reemplace, el juicio humano en la formación de competencias como el pensamiento crítico, la toma de decisiones, el debate argumentativo, la solución de problemas, el discernimiento ético, entre otras competencias propias de la profesión militar.</jats:p>

title: Aportes de la inteligencia artificial a la enseñanza de la memoria histórica en el sector defensa
container-title: La educación militar en la era digital: Nuevas herramientas y desafíos
3e5814c496eff2daf13c4983ddcc53e4f747fd76.abstract: <jats:p>En el escenario de post-conflicto que vive Colombia, la memoria histórica ha cobrado un papel central en la implementación del Sistema Integral de Verdad, Justicia, Reparación y No Repetición, el cual tiene la titánica labor de visibilizar, dignificar y reconocer a las víctimas del conflicto armado colombiano. Por tal motivo, su enseñanza resulta indispensable para que las generaciones centenials del sector defensa comprendan las causas, el desarrollo y las consecuencias del conflicto. El objetivo de este capítulo es analizar cómo la inteligencia artificial puede contribuir al aprendizaje de la memoria histórica, a través de un análisis documental y bibliométrico, sustentado en el modelo de aprendizaje constructivista, que permita identificar tendencias, enfoques y experiencias relevantes. Entre los principales hallazgos, se identificó un creciente interés investigativo en la articulación entre memoria histórica, tecnologías de aprendizaje e inteligencia artificial, que brindan oportunidades para el diseño de estrategias educativas más eficaces dirigidas a las nuevas generaciones.</jats:p>

title: Artificial intelligence for kinematic (procedural motion) analysis in gastrointestinal endoscopy: A systematic review
container-title: World Journal of Gastroenterology
b57da8d69347ef96ad6b53af36bb1108bb32c469.abstract:
<jats:p>BACKGROUND</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) in gastrointestinal endoscopy has focused on computer-aided detection (CADe) for recognition errors; AI addressing endoscope motion, coverage, workflow, and skill – collectively kinematic analysis – has not been systematically synthesized.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>AIM</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>To map kinematic AI evidence across eight predefined domains and assessed its quality relative to CADe and surgical AI.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>METHODS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>MEDLINE/PubMed, EMBASE-OVID, Cochrane, and IEEE Xplore were searched following Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses checklist (CRD420261320279). Studies applying AI to kinematic data in gastrointestinal endoscopy were eligible. Risk of bias used Cochrane Risk of Bias 2, Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies-2, and PROBAST + AI; certainty of evidence used GRADE.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>RESULTS</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Fifty-eight studies were included. Evidence generation was asymmetric: (1) Randomized controlled trial ratio approximately 5:1 (> 40 vs  8); (2) Patient ratio approximately 4:1 (> 27000 vs  approximately 6200); (3) Annual publication ratio approximately 12:1; and (4) ≥ 6 vs  0 regulatory approvals favoring diagnostic AI. Withdrawal speed monitoring and coverage/blind-spot mapping reached moderate GRADE certainty, but all 8 randomized controlled trials were from China and 6 of 8 used the ENDOANGEL platform. The remaining six domains have not reached moderate certainty: (1) Workflow recognition and skill assessment are approaching clinical readiness; and (2) Autonomous navigation, robotic control, simultaneous localization and mapping/three-dimensional reconstruction, and instrument tracking remain at the engineering stage. Comparison with surgical AI indicated that the gap reflects ecosystem-level factors – absence of open datasets, benchmarking challenges, and regulatory pathways for motion-acting AI – rather than technical immaturity.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>CONCLUSION</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Kinematic AI addresses exposure errors that CADe cannot correct and has shown additive benefit alongside CADe. Two domains are ready for geographically diverse validation; six remain at the engineering stage. Priorities are open datasets, benchmarking infrastructure, and dedicated regulatory pathways for motion-acting AI.</jats:p>

title: Beautiful Particulars
c6fe3d0377956ff06d423eb5e3d727284e365eac.abstract:
<jats:p>A fresh and eye-opening new explanation of AI—and how its focus on specifics is changing our ideas about ourselves and our world.From a Harvard researcher, philosopher, entrepreneur, former comedy writer, and bestselling author.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p>Amid the clamor about AI, Beautiful Particulars poses a unique question: Not how does our use of AI change what we do, but how is the idea of AI already subtly yet fundamentally reshaping how we think about ourselves and our world?</jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>
                  <jats:p>In clear, engaging, and even humorous prose, David Weinberger offers a new perspective on how machine learning works and how it may already be changing our basic and deepest ideas. Through lively examples, he shows that AI’s success—with all its risks and dangers—is taking us past our millennia of reliance on laws and principles by revealing what morality, free will, creativity, causality knowledge, and even reality itself look like now that we’re able to let the particulars speak their tiny truths.</jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>
                  <jats:p>The author poses questions not usually asked: What does a coin look like to AI? When AI gives you evidence that the earth is round, why are its own reasons for saying that so different? Why does an AI image generator create a “selfie” of ancient Aztec warriors with broad smiles that it “believes” are historically unlikely? If AI becomes conscious but bodiless, could it still make good moral decisions? Why is the world so much better at being causal than AI could ever “understand”? How does AI show us that genuine creativity is not about a “spark” but about moments that feel right? And how can you take the temperature of a joke?</jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>
                  <jats:p>Beautiful Particulars offers a new—and hopeful—perspective on how machine learning works, and how that’s already changing how we understand what it means to be human in the age of AI.</jats:p>

title: Masked denoising diffusion for accurate anomaly recognition and reconstruction
container-title: CAAI Artificial Intelligence Research
828c4288e3166ed63db2c3796155bc6efb0fa4e2.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>In data-driven industrial anomaly detection, the scarcity of defect samples and the emergence of unknown defect types pose significant challenges to quality control. While unsupervised generative models offer a viable solution, existing diffusion-based methods (e.g., DDAD) face a critical limitation: they often fail to distinguish between normal and anomalous patterns during reconstruction. Consequently, these models may inadvertently reconstruct the defects themselves rather than restoring the healthy state, leading to missed detections and inaccurate anomaly localization. To address this dilemma, we propose masked DDAD (mDDAD), which integrates masked image modeling (MIM) to enforce the learning of global semantic context, thereby enhancing sensitivity to anomalies. We further introduce a dynamic noise adjustment mechanism (DNAM) that selectively reduces noise intensity in masked regions to preserve essential structural information. Additionally, we optimize the training process via dynamic weighted loss optimization (DWLO) to prioritize critical regions. Experiments on the MVTec-AD and VisA datasets demonstrate that mDDAD effectively mitigates the reconstruction failure of baseline methods, significantly outperforming existing approaches in both anomaly detection and reconstruction accuracy. Code is available at https://github.com/zhg-SZPT/mDDAP.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Spillovers from Financial Distress and Bankruptcy: Evidence and Implications for the Real Economy
container-title: Annual Review of Financial Economics
f23821c612a17d9b8ddcf5e147c573b67f4a1021.abstract: <jats:p>Bankruptcy reallocates assets, labor, and risk across firms and households, yet its consequences extend far beyond the firms and households directly involved. This article reviews empirical and theoretical advances on spillovers from financial distress and bankruptcy—the transmission of financial distress through labor markets, product markets, supply chains, financial networks, and social interactions. We bring together evidence on how corporate bankruptcy affects workers, competitors, suppliers, and local economies, and how these effects aggregate to influence economic outcomes more broadly. We also highlight emerging evidence on consumer bankruptcy spillovers within peer and family networks. The literature consistently shows that these spillovers are substantial and operate through multiple channels. Throughout, we identify open questions about their welfare implications, the design of optimal bankruptcy policy, and opportunities to better characterize spillovers that have not yet been explored.</jats:p>

title: Institutional and economic factors in the development of the investment potential of Ukraine’s local communities
container-title: Actual problems of innovative economy and law
f2a0661c70b714455931c55b8017d6539e125e80.abstract:
<jats:p>This article examines the institutional and economic factors shaping and strengthening the investment potential of Ukraine’s territorial communities amid decentralization, reform of the public investment management system, and escalating security challenges. This study is relevant because local self-government bodies need stronger capacity to turn available resources into sound investment projects that develop the local economy, restore infrastructure, and ensure employment. This article aims to substantiate the institutional and economic factors underlying the enhancement of the investment potential of Ukraine’s territorial communities and to identify the sequence of management decisions that ensures the transformation of available resources into well-prepared investment projects. The study’s methodological basis consists of systemic and institutional approaches, as well as methods of analysis and synthesis, comparison, structural-functional systematization, and scientific generalization. The study distinguishes the economic meaning of investment potential, investment attractiveness, and investment activity in local communities. It has been established that the effectiveness of investment activity depends not only on the territory’s resource endowment but also on the legal and infrastructural readiness of assets, the quality of management procedures, human resource capacity, financial stability, and effective project management. The informational, institutional, infrastructural, human resource, financial, and security barriers to realizing investment potential have been systematized, and management tools for overcoming them have been identified. The need to coordinate public and private investments has been substantiated, accounting for differences in their financing mechanisms and common prerequisites for territorial development. This paper proposes a multi-criteria system for assessing local communities’ investment readiness, covering resource-economic, information-communication, institutional-legal, infrastructure, organizational-project, financial-budgetary, security-risk, and performance-monitoring components. The paper demonstrates the advisability of creating an individual profile of a community’s investment readiness rather than mechanically applying universal integrated ratings.

Keywords: investment potential, local communities, investments, local economic development, public investments, institutional capacity, competitiveness, investment management, investment risks.</jats:p>

title: Artificial intelligence in autoimmune pancreatitis: Differentiating immunoglobulin G4-related pancreatitis from pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
container-title: Artificial Intelligence in Gastroenterology
3d411446276cb96d8e96c66b03ca0a17ab144585.abstract: <jats:p>Autoimmune pancreatitis (AIP), specifically the immunoglobulin G4-related type-1 variant, serves as a significant benign mimic of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). Focal or mass-forming AIP can manifest as obstructive jaundice, a pancreatic mass, ductal narrowing, weight loss, and elevated tumor markers that may resemble those of PDAC. Misdiagnosis can result in either unnecessary pancreatic surgery or delayed treatment for cancer. Artificial intelligence (AI), including radiomics, machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal decision-support systems, offers a possible solution for this diagnostic dilemma. AI-based imaging is able to extract quantitative characteristics from a variety of modalities, such as computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, diffusion-weighted imaging, positron emission tomography, and endoscopic ultrasonography that may not be apparent by visual inspection. Digital pathology and models combining radiological, serological, histological and clinical variables are also on the rise. Current data is limited by small retrospective single-center cohorts, uneven imaging techniques, dependency on segmentation, and the absence of adequate external validation. AI should be seen as a supplement, not a substitute, to the professional multidisciplinary assessment, boosting the risk classification, directing the tissue collection, and steroid trials, and avoiding unnecessary procedures without delaying PDAC diagnosis. Future research should target prospective multicenter validation, uniform datasets, improved explainability and therapeutically significant objectives.</jats:p>

title: AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
0cea04df1f33891ac6e61332b69e78c30652b6e1.abstract: <jats:p>News gathering, production, verification, and distribution have been reshaped—sometimes profoundly, sometimes quietly—by the growing presence of artificial intelligence and machine learning in broadcast operations. This chapter surveys the main areas where these technologies operate: automated news production, deepfake detection, audience analytics, recommender systems, and voice synthesis. It also examines ethical questions emerging in each domain. Drawing on recent scholarship across journalism studies, computer science, media ethics, and communication research, the chapter explores tensions between operational efficiency and journalistic integrity, between personalization and information diversity, and between AI-assisted verification and its vulnerability to synthetic content. A key theme is that productivity gains, though real, are not self-sustaining. Responsible deployment requires editorial oversight, effective governance, and transparent disclosure to audiences. The chapter concludes by outlining a research agenda for an information environment increasingly shaped by AI.</jats:p>

title: The Digital Transformation of Television Broadcasting Supported by Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
35b7dc9c798c6869d6eeb6921fd0c44c284f95bc.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the digital transformation brought about by artificial intelligence and machine learning technologies in television broadcasting within a conceptual and critical framework. It discusses how processes such as content production, automation, scheduling, audience measurement and personalisation have been reorganised through data-driven systems. Furthermore, by assessing the impacts of algorithmicisation on editorial independence, public accountability, transparency, privacy and accountability, the study argues that the future of television broadcasting is shaped not only by technical innovation but also by institutional and ethical choices.</jats:p>

title: The Future of Television
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
bff6f50e054390e2c139c80e7fb45824d6ff514a.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation are transforming the television and broadcast media industry by reshaping production workflows, distribution models, and audience engagement strategies. Intelligent systems are increasingly applied in automated content creation, smart studio operations, personalized recommendation services, and predictive audience analytics. These innovations enhance efficiency, reduce operational costs, and enable broadcasters to deliver more adaptive and customized viewing experiences across digital platforms. However, the growing integration of AI also raises important challenges related to ethical accountability, algorithmic bias, transparency, and workforce transformation. Human creativity, editorial judgment, and trust remain essential elements in ensuring responsible media practices. The future of television will depend on balancing technological innovation with human-centered values to build sustainable and socially meaningful broadcast ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Digital Television Platforms
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
054cd1bab132b082e3e6a31810c1cc1a1ff38db7.abstract: <jats:p>This study investigates how artificial intelligence–driven algorithms on digital television platforms transform the processes of cultural production, distribution, and consumption within the media ecosystem. Focusing on Netflix as a case study, it analyzes how algorithmic recommendation systems structure content visibility, shape user preferences, and reorganize audience behavior through data-driven mechanisms. Drawing on sociological theories of power and cultural production, the study conceptualizes algorithms not merely as technical tools but as socio-technical actors that establish new regimes of visibility and control. In this context, the notion of the “algorithmic field” is proposed to explain how platform-based systems redefine power relations, mediate cultural hierarchies, and reproduce structural inequalities. The findings suggest that digital platforms operate as influential intermediaries that both organize and govern cultural circulation in contemporary media environments.</jats:p>

title: From Broadcast to Platform Power
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
0039e4646b5f12e04840a5816064712c21fdb48a.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the transformation of Turkish television from a broadcast-centered system into a platform-based, datafied media ecology shaped by Netflix, BluTV, Exxen, and related streaming services. It argues that streaming in Turkey cannot be understood as a simple technological shift, because platforms entered a media system already defined by dizi exports, RTÜK regulation, broadcast scarcity, censorship pressures, and audience dissatisfaction with long-form television. Through case studies of The Protector, Ethos, BluTV, and Exxen, the chapter analyzes how platform commissioning, personalization, metadata, recommendation systems, and AI-assisted workflows reshape cultural visibility, editorial authority, and creative labor. The chapter also considers how state regulation and media capture complicate platform governance in Turkey. It concludes that Turkish television's future depends on balancing algorithmic efficiency, cultural specificity, regulatory pressure, and editorial responsibility.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence, Local Broadcasting, and the Logic of Innovation From the Periphery
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
993d09fe2a97e708c317641849a351071457e373.abstract: <jats:p>Drawing on a qualitative case study of Radio Kepulauan Seribu, this chapter examines how these tensions unfold within Indonesia's small-island broadcasting context. Rather than framing AI as a disruptive force that automates editorial work, the chapter advances the concept of guided augmentation, in which AI supports preparatory cognitive tasks while ethical judgment, contextual interpretation, and public responsibility remain human-centered. Through interviews and non-participant observation, the study demonstrates how AI adoption emerges from structural constraints, limited resources, and public service mandates rather than technological ambition. The findings challenge dominant, Global North–centric narratives of AI-driven media transformation by presenting small islands as sites of adaptive innovation and relational accountability. By reframing hybrid broadcasting as a stable, context-sensitive media configuration, the chapter contributes to broader debates on AI, ethics, and the future of broadcasting in community-oriented media ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Television
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
857bae5718eff00351eeae246d5c2a40314cac99.abstract: <jats:p>With the process of digitalization, television broadcasting has evolved into a data-driven, algorithmic structure through digital platform services. In this context, the use of artificial intelligence is regarded as a tool that increases efficiency in television broadcasting. However, gaining competitive advantage through algorithmic infrastructures and the commodification of viewer data create forms of algorithmic management. This study examines the transformation created by artificial intelligence in the field of television broadcasting through platformization shaped by data ownership, the reshaping of labor processes through automation, and algorithmic governmentality as the outcome of these processes. The fact that artificial intelligence produces transformations in relation to capital accumulation, labor regimes, data ownership, and ideological control makes it necessary to evaluate television broadcasting from a political-economic perspective.</jats:p>

title: Algorithmic Curatorial Shift
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
1559be582d93ad91c2a432d936327ea610496ff5.abstract: <jats:p>Television program scheduling has long been an exercise in editorial authority: decisions regarding which programs to air, when, and in what order have shaped viewer behavior, structured the revenue logic of commercial broadcasting, and reproduced the broader ideological and economic conditions of the broadcasting system. The integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning into broadcasting operations is restructuring this framework. Algorithmic tools are increasingly shaping audience forecasting, ad placement, content performance evaluation, and recommendation systems. Drawing on Raymond Williams' flow theory, gatekeeping theory, and platform capitalism, this chapter examines this transformation through the concept of algorithmic curatorial shift, the redistribution of editorial authority from human planning experts to algorithmic systems.</jats:p>

title: Personalized Broadcasting and Algorithmic Recommender Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
45211ebcedbc6bad1d33a282df18d35a0dac1227.abstract: <jats:p>This study examines the digital transformation of television broadcasting through personalized broadcasting and algorithmic recommender systems. It aims to explain how television has evolved from a linear medium into a data driven, platform centered, and algorithmically organized environment. The study discusses the conceptual foundations of personalized broadcasting and the main types of recommender systems, including content based, collaborative, and hybrid models. The findings show that these systems are not merely technical tools for content discovery, but socio technical mechanisms that shape audience experience, engagement, content visibility, and cultural circulation. The Netflix case further demonstrates that algorithmic personalization has become a strategic force that restructures media economies, influences user preferences, and redefines contemporary broadcasting practices.</jats:p>

title: Watching What You Want
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
d1ff86b30e4ee238eb295d1fbf660002d7278fc2.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines how algorithmic recommendation systems have become central to television broadcasting. Drawing on critical media theory, platform studies, and research, it argues artificial intelligence and machine learning reshaped relationships between broadcasters and audiences by shifting curation from human programmers to automated systems. It situates collaborative filtering, content-based filtering, and deep learning within debates on filter bubbles, cultural fragmentation, editorial responsibility, and the political economy of digital media. Treating recommendation as a categorical transformation, it addresses ethics, including transparency, bias, and viewer autonomy, reviews regulatory and self-governance frameworks, and outlines future trends such as emotion-aware AI and cross-platform personalization.</jats:p>

title: AI, Television News, and the Future of Democratic Gatekeeping
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
3ee3b8c7e6d4280704c4999714e0509349e034cd.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is increasingly shaping television news production by influencing how stories are selected, prioritized, and targeted to audiences. While AI offers efficiency and data-driven decision-making, it also raises concerns about democratic gatekeeping in broadcast journalism by challenging traditional ideas of editorial judgment, accountability, transparency, and pluralism. This chapter examines how AI reshapes gatekeeping in television news by shifting decisions from human editors to hybrid human-AI systems. Drawing on gatekeeping theory and journalism studies, it explores issues such as algorithmic opacity, automation bias, and reduced diversity in news coverage. The chapter argues that without proper governance, AI-assisted gatekeeping may weaken the democratic role of television news. To address these concerns, it proposes a framework for democratic gatekeeping in AI-assisted television news based on transparency, human oversight, editorial responsibility, and pluralism, offering guidance for integrating AI into news workflows.</jats:p>

title: The Transformation of News Discourse in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Machine Learning in Broadcast Media
8e94f02ed0fdcf254c98a1451e802610a07e5039.abstract: <jats:p>In the digital media ecosystem, AI-based text generation systems, particularly large language models, have become increasingly influential in news production processes. These systems are viewed not only as technical tools but also as new mechanisms of discourse production that reshape how news content is created. This development has made the comparative examination of human-produced and AI-generated news texts increasingly important. In this context, the study comparatively analyzes news texts selected from international news organizations such as Al Jazeera and Reuters alongside texts generated by ChatGPT. The research focuses on military interventions and violent incidents in Palestine. Using document analysis as a qualitative research method, the study evaluates the texts through Teun A. van Dijk's Critical Discourse Analysis approach and identifies major differences between human-produced and AI-generated news texts in terms of discourse structure, framing strategies, linguistic choices, and meaning production practices.</jats:p>

title: Inclusive Cognitive Design for Global Workforce
container-title: Creative Advantage of Cultural Diversity in Global Business
3c9423f36ac85a9387994c325c3b8405da65dee9.abstract: <jats:p>This paper combines microlearning and inclusivity by suggesting a cognitive design framework that deals with unstable memory at the organizational level. Precarious memory is infrequently addressed in organizational research. This study integrates cognitive science, instructional frameworks, and diversity practices while examining the challenges encountered in VUCA workforce environments. Microlearning as the primary mechanism, facilitated by cultural intelligence and bias awareness, results in task agility and is regulated by psychological safety. The research demonstrates the substantial effectiveness of microlearning in mitigating fragile memory. The results indicate that unstable memory and memory distortion can be trained and alleviated using the proposed framework. This framework makes things more fair and equal and less biased in the workplace. Microlearning's modular approach connects learning with making good decisions, which helps create a workplace that is fair and ethical.</jats:p>

title: Ethical Leadership in Diversity
container-title: Creative Advantage of Cultural Diversity in Global Business
7a7f4cb96cdb61c67e5dc72818677d4ce23d0150.abstract: <jats:p>In the twenty-first century, as societies and organizations become increasingly multicultural, ethical leadership stands as a vital force in shaping inclusive and equitable environments. This chapter examines how leadership rooted in integrity, empathy, justice, accountability, and cultural adaptability can move diversity beyond compliance toward a meaningful human commitment. While many institutions formally endorse inclusion, practices often remain limited by unconscious bias, tokenism, and superficial engagement. Addressing these gaps requires a leadership approach that blends ethical values with cultural awareness. Drawing on established theoretical perspectives, the chapter presents a Five-Pillar Framework of Ethical Leadership designed for diverse contexts. It illustrates this framework through global examples, highlighting how ethical leadership adapts across cultures and sectors. The chapter also identifies key barriers and offers practical strategies for embedding ethical principles into organizational practices.</jats:p>

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Sustainable Business Practices
container-title: Creative Advantage of Cultural Diversity in Global Business
090db250767a4ce195bc4d60239e9576465403ae.abstract: <jats:p>Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) has strategized environmental, economic and social sustainability into its operations as well as in innovation endeavours. CSR practices motivate the green sustainable operations by eliminating harmful effects. The current study tries to examine the CSR strategies helps in promoting sustainable business practices advancing cultural diversity and creative advantage. Further, it investigates the fundamental pillars of CSR and align it with effective CSR strategies. Lastly, it explores the challenges and opportunities organizations faced while implementation of effective CSR strategies. The present study is descriptive and imperative in nature utilizing three case studies from Tesla, Patagonia and Unilever in order to suffice the research questions. The study discusses the policy implication in respect to the varied stakeholders strengthening the CSR regulation, implementation and foster sustainability initiatives. Therefore, encompassing CSR into institution curriculum will enhance succeeding success, competitive advantage and resilience.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Harmony
container-title: Innovative Strategies for Well-Being and Motivation in Education
010b400f9132cfa7bf09958baa6e7f8172d8af52.abstract: <jats:p>Previous research has shown how motivation and anxiety affect students' academic success, which highlights the importance of implementing strategies in the classroom to promote motivation and manage anxiety in students. Despite these findings, there is a lack of research offering practical guidelines for applying this knowledge in the classrooms. Therefore, the need arises to identify and compile educational strategies and practices that teachers can implement in the classroom to foster motivation and control their students' anxiety. In this chapter, we conducted a literature review aimed at compiling, from an educational scientific evidence approach, various interventions and teaching strategies to promote learning achievement through motivation and anxiety management.</jats:p>

title: AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

title: “Friendship” and “Love” With Companion Robots
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
022fceef735cce777f0d8dacf51096f466dfc905.abstract: <jats:p>The emergence of companion robots introduces profound questions about the nature of human relationships, specifically regarding friendship and love. Unlike conventional machines, these robots are designed to provide emotional support, social interaction, and even intimacy, blurring the boundaries between human and artificial companionship. This paper explores the psychological, ethical, and societal implications of forming such bonds. It investigates the drivers behind these attachments including loneliness, accessibility, and advances in AI realism and examines whether these relationships can be considered authentic. The study also assesses potential benefits, such as improved mental well-being, alongside challenges like dependency, ethical concerns, and broader societal acceptance. By analyzing theoretical frameworks, real-world applications, and future trajectories, this work offers a holistic understanding of how companion robots are reshaping fundamental human experiences like friendship and love in contemporary life.</jats:p>

title: Human Socialization (and Dis-Socialization) by AI and Robotic Companions in Educational Ecosystems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
21e354c94bb2573462d54359bd698db08de31a01.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter interrogates how AI chatbots, social robots, and ambient agents function as companion technologies that reconfigure human socialization and dis-socialization in educational ecosystems. Drawing on socialization theory, ecological systems, sociocultural mediation, sociomaterial assemblages, and posthuman subjectivity, it constructs a multi-level lens spanning micro interactional dynamics, meso institutional architectures, and macro political economies. The chapter develops typologies of companion configurations, maps learner needs to companion affordances, and analyses interactional quality through constructs such as social presence, parasociality, and epistemic justice. It then articulates normative, rights-based, and governance frameworks that distribute responsibilities across learners, educators, institutions, vendors, regulators, and civil society. The chapter positions humane companionable education as an agenda that seeks to harness machine companionship for inclusion and flourishing while resisting surveillance, stratification, and civic erosion.</jats:p>

title: Aesthetics of Robotic Digital Pets
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
7e635f747fbbe5476f902f978891bbe7c498f00f.abstract: <jats:p>Robots designed to replace pets are being developed to meet the emotional, social and cognitive needs of different age groups, from children to seniors. This chapter analyzes the factors that influence people's perception of robotic pets as companionable and socially present, focusing on shape aesthetics and motion quality, sound quality and textural effects and behavioral patterns. By examining the history of how humans have created and used artificial beings, it also becomes possible to understand how aesthetics has been viewed in the past and how it continues to shape expectations for the future. User expectations regarding the design of artificial pets, as well as the personalization of these products, are shown to influence acceptance and engagement. Understanding the role of aesthetics in the development of artificial pets therefore supports the creation of ethical and meaningful companions within contemporary and global society.</jats:p>

title: Emotional and Social Intelligence in AI Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
6a2e01dfa5708795013bf97dce0351890b7ec891.abstract: <jats:p>As artificial intelligence increasingly engages emotional and social dimensions of human life, its ability to recognize and respond to emotion raises important ethical and philosophical concerns. This chapter examines the development of emotional and social intelligence in AI, highlighting the shift from rational computation toward affective interaction. Drawing on cognitive psychology, affective computing, and moral philosophy, it explores whether machine empathy reflects genuine understanding or performative simulation. The discussion addresses risks such as emotional surveillance, manipulation, dependency, and cultural misrecognition, while acknowledging benefits of emotionally responsive AI in education, healthcare, and assistive contexts. To address ethical gaps, the chapter proposes a Computational Compassion Framework (CCF) integrating moral intentionality, transparency, human oversight, and contextual sensitivity into AI design. It argues that the future of emotional AI lies not in humanizing machines, but in embedding ethical responsibility within technological systems.</jats:p>

title: Iron Man or Tin Man?
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
739e5ce062b70ab12c4e4d9faa2f7e77bf9b8104.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence and robotics are no longer distant technologies but intimate infrastructures of everyday life, shaping how humans think, decide, feel, and relate to time, data, and one another.Drawing on cultural allegories (the Tin Man as the loss of emotional agency, Iron Man as the promise and peril of augmentation, In Time as a warning about the commodification of time, and the contemporary data economy where habit itself becomes a product) this chapter argues that the central challenge of AI is not technological capability, but human capacity. Through interdisciplinary perspectives from communication studies, psychology, and critical AI ethics, the analysis reveals how persuasion, efficiency, and optimization quietly reshape human behavior without overt coercion. Rather than asking whether machines can become more human, this chapter reframes the question: can humans remain reflective, empathetic, and morally responsible in systems designed for speed and prediction?</jats:p>

title: The Human Side of Robotic Warehousing
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
49ef72dbd7010ac0048e4e4ae894fc8d134c1a59.abstract: <jats:p>The chapter explores the perceptions of employees working in Amazon's Robotic Mobile Fulfillment Systems (RMFS). We used a netnographic approach to uncover employees' perceptions related to the use of this technology, as well as the social and ethical considerations related to the topic. The results of the study show several advantages perceived by the employees in terms of flexibility, improved picking rates, and ergonomics at work. Nevertheless, numerous risks and challenges emerged from the qualitative analysis conducted specifically in relation to job security and human-machine interaction. The results and analyses offer us several perspectives regarding the automation and robotization of workspaces in relation to employees' perceptions and social considerations.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Emotion, Social Intelligence, and Culture in Robotic Companions
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
11b5a43f16d9978c902b26af103395a866acf26f.abstract: <jats:p>The chapter discusses how emotional, social and cultural intelligence can be integrated into the design of robotic companions and their importance in promoting authentic, empathetic and adaptive human-machine relationships. It explores theoretical assumptions, technology methods, and examples of the application of emotional recognition, social adaptability, and cultural sensitivity. The most notable challenges mentioned in the discussion include ethical dilemmas, trust, and cross-cultural differences, as well as determine the way forward as influenced by affective computing, cultural AI, and large language models. Finally, the chapter encourages an integrated system that incorporates human compassion and machine predictability to increase emotional resonance, inclusivity, and universal acceptance in human socialization with AI.</jats:p>

title: Ethical Dimensions of Companion Bots, Intelligent Devices, and Artificial Intelligence
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI and Robotic Companions for Human Socialization
3244f1bc2f7abb55a5b6321434f09e48bbe95961.abstract: <jats:p>Companion bots and emotionally responsive AI systems integrate deeply into daily life, managing social interactions, emotional support, learning, and care. Unlike standard computational tools, they maintain ongoing relationships and mimic empathy, transforming perceptions of companionship, autonomy, and moral responsibility. They deliver key benefits like alleviating loneliness, advancing healthcare, and customizing education, but raise ethical issues around authenticity, dependency, privacy, manipulation, and accountability. This chapter explores these ethics through philosophy, human-computer interaction (HCI), psychology, and policy lenses. It contends that evaluations must go beyond utility to examine effects on human dignity, moral agency, and social values. Principles for ethical design, governance, and deployment follow, emphasizing human well-being amid AI companionship's moral stakes .</jats:p>

title: Harnessing Digital Platforms and Artificial Intelligence for Quality Assurance and Monitoring
container-title: Harnessing Digital Platforms for Quality Assurance and Monitoring in Higher Education
6492aae0c96a95ea65d135b36278e404e91578e1.abstract: <jats:p>Digital transformation: a paradigmatic shift toward data-driven and AI-supported academic excellence in higher education quality assurance. In this chapter, we offer a holistic framework for leveraging the power of digital platforms and AI technologies to enhance quality assurance and monitoring in HEIs. Combining systematic literature review, theoretical framework development, and empirical analysis through correlation analysis,  regression modeling, and structural equation modeling (SEM), we define the essential building blocks for implementing appropriate digital QA systems. This framework integrates various data points, predictive analytics, machine learning algorithms, and real-time monitoring capabilities to deliver a comprehensive solution for managing academic quality. Concrete data points include strong, positive correlations between digital platform use and quality, and regression analysis shows that AI-enhanced monitoring systems account for a 23.7% improvement in these indicators. Results of SEM confirmed the proposed framework, with good fit indices.</jats:p>

title: Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

title: Governing AI-Driven Universities in Cambodia
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
1c876c30e971c0906955347a760678450910f5f3.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter focuses on Cambodian higher education institutions to explain the pillars of Trust-Centred AI Governance for responsible AI and how AI can support services and functions currently burdened by demand and under-resourced in the Cambodian higher education sector, which is rapidly growing and flexible in enrollment. Without governance, the Threats to Educational Equity caused by algorithmic bias, Data Breaches, Digital Exclusion, and Breaches of Trust will dangerously flourish. This chapter presents a Trust-Centred AI Governance Framework built around seven principles: ethical leadership, transparency, and data privacy. It is supported by core ideas such as algorithmic accountability, inclusive access, human oversight, and public-sector innovation, and guides partner institutions on fostering ethical innovation ecosystems. It presents, through analyses and the implementation of proposed strategies, case studies, and policy frameworks, a model that balances technological efficiency with human-centred principles, empowering global competence and leadership in the south.</jats:p>

title: From Knowledge Transmission to Democratic Transformation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
14a3b3c15207f76fff58adce5bfb961062efee1c.abstract: <jats:p>The rapidly evolving context of digitalisation, democratic fragility, and educational inequality has highlighted the need to change conventional teacher education practices that focus on transmission of knowledge and skills. Although teacher identity is a key concept in contemporary educational reform discussions that focus on inclusion, digital innovation and democratic citizenship, the concept is still fractured in policy, curriculum and governance. This research faces this challenge and critically explores the changing landscape of teacher education in terms of reconstructing the teacher identity as a multidimensional and transformative professional construct to support democratic transformation. In this study, the doctrinal and analytical research methodology is used, which systematically reviews and synthesizes the current educational theories, international policy instruments, governance models, and scholarly debates on inclusive education, digital pedagogy, democratic citizenship and professional development.</jats:p>

title: Integrating Internet of Things and Artificial Intelligence for the Development of Sustainable, Intelligent, and Efficient Physical–Digital Learning
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
26c5b42ef86ad41f27f523603793d198bf2cb6ce.abstract: <jats:p>The application of the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial intelligence (AI) is driving towards a new era of intelligent, adaptive, and sustainable smart campus ecosystems in higher education institutions. This research aims to examine the potential of IoT-powered physical–digital learning environments and AI systems in the fields of personalized learning, intelligent campus management, predictive analytics, and sustainable resource optimization. The study also explores the opportunities and challenges associated with the application of AIoT technologies for enhancing operational efficiency, learner participation, and environmental sustainability, as well as those of cybersecurity, data privacy, interoperability, and ethical governance. The results emphasize the need to implement human-centered, secure, and sustainable technological frameworks to empower future-ready universities and foster inclusive, efficient, and resilient educational ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Shadows in the Lecture Hall
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
66561a07cf91a6cd744b035edb6f73babf583b22.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial Intelligence has rapidly transitioned from a supporting tool to a central force in academic research, teaching, and institutional governance. Its capacity to process vast datasets, generate scholarly content, and enhance decision-making offers unprecedented opportunities for innovation. Universities now employ AI to streamline administrative operations, improve academic workflows, and enable personalized learning experiences. In research, advanced algorithms and large language models facilitate literature synthesis, data interpretation, and even hypothesis generation, thereby accelerating scholarly output. This chapter advances the argument that the future of academia depends on striking a careful equilibrium between embracing AI's transformative power and preserving the foundational principles of truth, fairness, and accountability. It proposes a framework for “Responsible AI in Academia” grounded in transparency, inclusivity, and continuous ethical evaluation.</jats:p>

title: Responsible AI Governance Frameworks for Intelligent Higher Education Management and Creative Public Sector Innovation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
99d99fa7c05bdbaa0acde5b32467be06597babd5.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines responsible AI governance for intelligent higher education management and public-sector innovation. It highlights the importance of ethical AI, governance transparency, institutional readiness, stakeholder AI literacy, and sustainability-oriented governance in AI-enabled ecosystems. The study proposes a conceptual governance framework integrating ethical oversight, intelligent decision-support systems, governance interoperability, and adaptive governance mechanisms. The chapter also discusses governance challenges associated with generative AI, including algorithmic bias, explainability, misinformation, and compliance risks. The findings emphasize that responsible AI governance supports sustainable institutional transformation, public trust, accountability, and human-centred innovation across higher education and public-sector environments.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Adaptation and Leadership in AI-Augmented Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
a5612c037c0c5391ee895bba1a4fc5ae65f530b1.abstract: <jats:p>Generative AI poses pressing governance challenges regarding the future of human-AI interaction and how it enhances or diminishes the cognitive capabilities, professional role, and leadership of academic professionals. Three cognitive adaptation patterns emerge from the analysis of the qualitative data (retrieved from the interviews) and the quantitative data (PLS-SEM survey): AI Augmentation, AI Dependency, and AI Co-construction. The positive relationship between adaptation outcomes and AI trust is supported by PLS-SEM, with the cognitive load change as a mediator and the organisational learning orientation as a moderator, the most significant institutional factor influencing adaptation outcomes. The chapter suggests embedding metacognition and AI literacy in workforce governance, institutional reflection in HR and L&D processes, and complementarity guardrails. For practical governance tools for adopting responsible AI in higher education, a validated diagnostic instrument and a Human-AI Capability Convergence Model are provided.</jats:p>

title: Transforming Academic Governance in the AI Era
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
e49d653e589a416eb7de0e2ea2a3cdd823c5f09a.abstract: <jats:p>Generative AI (GAI) has rapidly become an integral part of higher education, significantly reshaping the teaching, learning, assessment, and research experiences of institutions around the globe, thereby creating unprecedented moral, legal, and governance dilemmas. Academic honesty and honour codes, which typically aimed to combat cheating and plagiarism in human-powered settings, are no longer adequate to deal with the challenges of AI-enabled environments. The study critically reviews the current paradigm of academic governance in the context of the emergence of generative AI and addresses the interplay of institutional honour codes, ethical responsibility, accountability systems, and regulatory compliance in higher education institutions. The research is done by a doctrinal, interdisciplinary and policy-oriented approach, analysing new institutional polices on AI, international ethical guidelines, university governance frameworks, data protection laws, and current academic discussions on responsible use of AI in academia.</jats:p>

title: AI Governance in Academia
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Responsible AI Governance in Higher Education Management for Creative Public Sector Innovation
82978771df486b7a50f02bfe7e3688784c7559c6.abstract: <jats:p>The ability to add artificial intelligence (AI) to higher education institutions in the entire public sector has opened up never-before opportunities to personalised learning, administrative efficiency and evidence-based policy-making. However, such opportunities are kept in company with serious governance issues that relate to transparency, fairness and institutional accountability. The chapter examines ethical strains that are inherent in utilisation of AI systems in the evaluation of students, collection of admission details, and distribution of resources, and argues that without the presence of robust governance architectures these systems have a risk of entrenching the existing inequalities and also eroding democratic educational values. The chapter is based on a multi-layered governance model which incorporates regulatory compliance, stakeholder participation, algorithmic auditing, and continuous ethics oversight.</jats:p>

title: Artificial intelligence in digestive diseases: Current evidence and clinical perspectives
container-title: Artificial Intelligence in Gastroenterology
9a41bb246ff98e522e359e943fa390fc82d2e66b.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming the field of gastroenterology, providing new ways to diagnose, risk-stratify, and therapeutically manage a wide variety of gastrointestinal diseases. Machine learning and deep learning algorithms are among the AI-based models that have shown promise in non-invasive fibrosis assessment, early detection of hepatocellular carcinoma, prediction of disease severity in pancreatitis, and polyp detection during endoscopy. We searched major databases, including Scopus, EMBASE, PubMed/MEDLINE, and Web of Science, and analyzed current studies on AI in gastroenterology. The integration of AI with imaging modalities, electronic health records, and multi-omics data has led to greater diagnostic accuracy and individualized patient care. Yet, these advances have not addressed issues of data quality, algorithm generalizability, interpretability, and clinical integration. Future research will focus on prospective validation of AI, regulation, and implementation to maximize the clinical utility of AI in digestive diseases. AI has the potential to improve patient outcomes, enable personalized medicine, and optimize the overall efficiency of processes involved in gastroenterological care. In this paper, recent literature concerning the use of AI in gastrointestinal endoscopy and the treatment of various gastrointestinal disorders, such as liver and pancreatic diseases, inflammatory bowel disease, and malignancies, was reviewed.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy–Based Digital Interventions for Illicit Substance Use Disorders: Scoping Review of Intervention Design, Efficacy Indicators, and Methodological Gaps
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
9d1858cff34c91ccfc45c7d996e799804ca90d99.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Illicit substance use disorders (SUDs) are escalating globally; yet, social stigma and legal barriers restrict access to conventional treatment, and existing research remains skewed toward alcohol and nicotine. Digital interventions incorporating cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) offer a discreet, scalable alternative.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="objective">
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This scoping review maps how CBT-based digital interventions for illicit SUDs are designed and delivered across platforms, identifying their theoretical frameworks, functional components, outcome indicators, and reported methodological limitations.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="methods">
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>We followed the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) scoping review methodology and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews). Six databases (PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, APA PsycINFO, Web of Science Core Collection, Cochrane Library, and CINAHL) were searched from inception to June 28, 2026, without language, date, or study design limits, supplemented by backward and forward citation searching (July 3, 2026). Eligible studies were empirical primary studies quantitatively evaluating digital interventions incorporating CBT for illicit or nonprescribed substance use; alcohol- or nicotine-only populations were excluded. Three reviewers independently screened and charted all studies, with disagreements resolved by consensus or adjudication. Data were synthesized narratively, with tables, figures, and an evidence gap map.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="results">
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Fifty-six studies published between 2008 and 2026, drawn from 47 distinct participant samples, met the eligibility criteria. Most were conducted in North America (40/56, 71.4%) and used randomized controlled designs (39/56, 69.6%). Polysubstance-using populations were most frequently targeted (32/56, 57.1%), followed by cannabis (13/56, 23.2%), opioids (6/56, 10.7%), and stimulants (5/56, 8.9%). Interventions were delivered mainly via web (24/56, 42.9%) or app (24/56, 42.9%) platforms, and most (49/56, 87.5%) were grounded in traditional CBT, most often combined with contingency management (18/56, 32.1%) or motivational interviewing (17/56, 30.4%). Core functional components included therapeutic intervention (55/56, 98.2%), self-tracking and notification (25/56, 44.6%), reward (24/56, 42.9%), and support and feedback (21/56, 37.5%). Primary outcomes focused on substance use and abstinence (41/56, 73.2%), retention/feasibility (16/56, 28.6%), and mental health status or coping skills (14/56, 25%). Author-reported limitations were predominantly participant-level (52/56, 92.9%), measurement-level (43/56, 76.8%), study-level (34/56, 60.7%), and intervention-level (25/56, 44.6%) domains.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="conclusions">
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Unlike previous reviews confined to a single substance or delivery platform, this review is innovative in mapping CBT-based digital interventions across the full spectrum of illicit substances, including polysubstance use, and in linking their functional components to intended therapeutic mechanisms. It thereby contributes to the development of these technologies and, by synthesizing author-reported limitations, proposes methodological improvements for their future evaluation. At present, CBT-based digital interventions are best positioned as adjuncts that extend the reach and continuity of existing addiction care rather than as stand-alone substitutes for it; substance-specific customization, objective outcome measures, and modular trial designs are needed to establish them as scalable clinical tools.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Disruption Forecasting and Predictive Analytics With Machine Learning Approaches
