17c3410fca5d52334564908f9163fcfe7cb92222.abstract: <jats:p>This research addresses predictive analytics for proactive risk identification and management across sectors. Using time series analysis, ML algorithms, and Chi-square testing, the study found that financial forecasting models are accurate, with credit scoring models being 85% accurate. The study reveals that predictive analytics-based frameworks considerably improve an organization's resilience. To boost forecast accuracy, businesses should integrate real-time data, use adaptive algorithms, and customise models for their sector. ML-based predictive analytics can forecast, plan for, and reduce these issues. This chapter discusses ML in predictive analytics and how firms may leverage data-driven insights to become more resilient and ready for anything. ML approaches including supervised learning, unsupervised clustering, and DL architectures are examined for disruption prediction. Real-world examples demonstrate how things work, and discussions of challenges and trends encourage research and industry use.</jats:p>

title: AI Crisis Simulations for Strategic Supply Chain Resilience Engineering
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
efa3bdd3f378e0abf94485b4112923a7db9e1877.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores the integration of Scenario Intelligence (SI) in supply chain resilience engineering, leveraging AI-powered simulations for crisis management. Traditional risk management approaches are increasingly ineffective at addressing modern, unpredictable disruptions, whereas SI, through dynamic AI-driven simulations, enables proactive, real-time decision-making. Theoretical frameworks like complexity theory and resilience engineering—evolving from robustness to antifragility—are central to understanding the adaptability of supply chains in crises. The chapter covers practical applications of AI simulations in predicting and managing natural disasters, pandemics, and geopolitical risks, demonstrating how AI enhances decision-making in volatile environments. It also highlights the role of policy frameworks, industry innovations, and global governance in fostering AI adoption for resilience. Despite its potential, challenges such as data privacy, integration complexities, and governance issues remain significant barriers.</jats:p>

title: AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility Health Crises, Geopolitical Strife, and Cyber-Sabotage
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
4614f38b11f4dc792498ad9446a4ebd70c22f00e.abstract: <jats:p>The threat of unparalleled disruptions of international supply chains caused by health crises (example, COVID-19), geopolitical and geo economic tensions, and an increase in the risk of cyber-sabotage is growing. The conventional risk management strategies are not sufficient in handling the multi-dimensional nature of supply chains today. This chapter explores the potential uses of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in securing, stabilizing and future-proofing supply chains in the face of volatile conditions. By combining predictive analytics with blockchain, machine learning-driven anomaly forecasting, and the use of AI-driven decision-support tools, companies can also ensure resilience against uncertainty, cyberattack, and breakdowns in logistical operations. The chapter also examines how the incorporation of AI and supply chain governance connect in terms of ethics, and how to protect data security. By integrating a set of conceptual frameworks, real-life industry case studies and best practices within global supply chains</jats:p>

title: Cybersecurity in Digital Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
a2d591ae29b63d49c8f5b0f24754dec3ea764c2d.abstract: <jats:p>With ever-increasing exposures of interconnected networks to threats and complex vulnerabilities, the cybersecurity of digital supply chains acquires importance. The principle of zero-trust architecture is, never trust always verify. An implication of this is that stringent authentication must be validated, real-time acknowledgment and monitoring must be ensured at all points, and the least-privilege access must be granted to all the users and devices. An undeniable fact is that blockchain guarantees security in transactions through its decentralized and tamper-proof record. Thus, building a truly trust less infrastructure in logistics and supply chain, blockchain and smart contract-based applications can be employed to automate business processes, remove intermediaries, and prevent fraud. For a quantum computer, post-quantum cryptography becomes an answer to preserve secrets in view of any threat of decryption; it thereby replaces classical ways of encryption with one that resists quantum attack.</jats:p>

title: AI-Driven Supply Chain Security
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
a9fac601cba8221d0a0ca6b6ee0491173add368e.abstract: <jats:p>Supply chains are the backbone of global trade, yet they face unprecedented risks in the digital era. Integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into supply chain security has emerged as a transformative strategy to manage complex risks, enhance cyber defenses, and build resilient networks. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of how AI is reshaping supply chain risk management, from predicting disruptions to automating responses. It discusses how AI-driven tools bolster cybersecurity in increasingly digital supply chains, identifying threats and safeguarding critical links. The chapter also examines the ethical challenges—such as data privacy, bias, and accountability—arising from AI integration, along with governance measures to ensure responsible use. Policy and international cooperation aspects are explored, recognizing that global supply chains require harmonized regulations and collaboration.</jats:p>

title: Architecting Antifragile Supply Chains With AI, Digital Twins, and Zero Trust Architecture
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
633ea892d6852074e94cf9336e159d7797152a41.abstract: <jats:p>In an era defined by perpetual disruption, traditional supply chain models have proven dangerously fragile. This chapter introduces the “Sentient Shield,” a novel framework for architecting antifragile supply chains that benefit from disruptions rather than merely withstanding them. The framework integrates three critical technologies: AI driven predictive analytics for precognition, Digital Twins for hyper realistic visualization and simulation, and Zero Trust Architectures as a foundational security posture. Through detailed case studies of the COVID 19 vaccine distribution, semiconductor trade wars, and the SolarWinds cyberattack, this chapter demonstrates how the Sentient Shield creates supply chains that learn from disruption. The chapter concludes with practical implementation principles and discusses governance challenges, providing a comprehensive blueprint for C suite leaders, government strategists, and researchers seeking to build self-improving supply networks in an increasingly volatile global environment.</jats:p>

title: Securing Supply Chain Data Integrity
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
6ae06d7ba4e33764ea4e2c6baf465dcb9f47235f.abstract: <jats:p>The digitization of global supply chains has enhanced efficiency but simultaneously expanded the attack surface for cyber-sabotage and insider manipulation. Ensuring data integrity across interconnected entities has become a strategic necessity for operational resilience. This chapter presents an AI-driven multi-layered framework integrating machine learning, deep learning, federated learning, and explainable AI to strengthen data authenticity and transparency. The framework detects behavioral and contextual anomalies, preserves privacy through decentralized intelligence, and supports auditability via interpretable decision outputs. Analytical case studies from pharmaceutical and semiconductor domains demonstrate adaptability across heterogeneous supply environments. The study further outlines future research directions involving quantum-safe architectures, sustainable AI, and ethical governance, positioning artificial intelligence as a cornerstone for secure, trustworthy, and resilient supply chain ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: The Convergence of National Security and Supply Chain Sovereignty
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
AI-Secured Supply Chains Amid Global Volatility
44cb6bda4d1590b2dfc8114ac6a80fe1ec18625f.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in global supply chains has reshaped how organizations and governments predict, detect, and respond to security threats. Yet, this transformation has produced both notable successes and critical failures. This book explores real-world adoption cases, best practices from multinational corporations and defense agencies, and the regulatory, ethical, and technological challenges influencing AI integration. It also projects the future of supply chain sovereignty in 2040 and beyond, highlighting risks such as technological dependency, data monopolization, and geopolitical fragmentation. By combining insights from policy, industry, and technology, the book offers a comprehensive framework for securing supply chains and provides guidance for academics, policymakers, and practitioners seeking to align AI innovation with resilience, ethics, and long-term security.</jats:p>

Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
34de16ba31a98b6ca3895143b1aa9ee703bcb69c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines three technology families that have drawn attention from supply chain researchers and practitioners: blockchain, augmented and virtual reality (AR/VR), and edge computing. The argument is not simply that each yields operational benefits, but that their significance lies in addressing complementary problems within a single domain. Blockchain addresses trust and information integrity in multi-party networks; AR/VR addresses human interface challenges in complex environments; edge computing provides distributed computation enabling real-time responsiveness at scale. Drawing on recent work, the chapter traces how these technologies support the industrial metaverse. Sustainability, resilience, human-centred design, and infrastructure scalability are key themes. It also examines challenges—interoperability, governance gaps, cost barriers, and security exposures—and offers a coherent view of their convergence and implications.</jats:p>

title: Industrial Metaverse in Supply Chain Management
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
09f40adbf7cb76bff382bbf6d92aec1c8a0bac82.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the concept of the industrial metaverse in supply chain management, highlighting its role in enabling AI-driven virtualization, collaborative decision-making, and sustainable transformation. It explores how technologies such as artificial intelligence, digital twins, IoT, and immersive interfaces create integrated, real-time, and interactive supply chain ecosystems. The study emphasizes the shift from reactive to predictive and autonomous supply chains through simulation, optimization, and data-driven intelligence. It further discusses the role of the industrial metaverse in enhancing multi-stakeholder collaboration, operational efficiency, and environmental sustainability through circular economy practices. A comprehensive framework is proposed to integrate technological, organizational, and strategic dimensions. The chapter contributes by offering insights into building resilient, intelligent, and sustainable supply chain systems.</jats:p>

title: Digital Twin Architecture in Supply Chain Systems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
d99b6055016f0e8c84e8e502fe276ebb105bc5e1.abstract: <jats:p>The major gap that still exists is the operationalization of the application of the concept of digital twist in the supply chain management although more research has been done on the area. This is more so in the emerging countries where its adoption is impeded by infrastructural and fragmented logistic ecosystems and limited capital. This chapter addresses that gap by introducing digital twin architectures within supply chain processes through a structured conceptual framework to support adaptive governance, anticipate risks, and intelligence in decision-making. Three basic mechanisms are discussed in the chapter such as (1) bi-directional data synchronization in real-time among supply chain nodes; (2) predictive simulation modeling of demand volatility and disruption; and (3) cross-tier visibility as an architecture requirement of coordination. These processes rest on a critical review of the literature, industry experience and systems-thinking concepts.</jats:p>

title: Cognitive Digital Twins and Blockchain Ecosystems
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
800c4603905b0b481af418f93c27b335627b538c.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter develops an architecture for combining cognitive digital twins with blockchain ecosystems to deliver predictive business intelligence in the industrial metaverse. It argues that digital-twin initiatives create value only when operational telemetry, semantic context, decision models, and human governance are connected through trusted data-sharing and executable coordination mechanisms. Drawing on research in digital twins, industrial metaverse design, blockchain-enabled provenance, smart contracts, human-centric manufacturing, and explainable AI, the chapter proposes a layered reference architecture, performance metrics, implementation logic, and governance controls. It also examines persistent challenges, including semantic fragmentation, model drift, latency, privacy, interoperability, energy cost, and the oracle problem. The chapter concludes with design recommendations and a research agenda for resilient, trustworthy, and economically useful industrial intelligence systems across networked industrial-metaverse platforms and ecosystems.</jats:p>

title: Digital Twins and Blockchain-Enabled Trust for Resilient Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
6cae48cda77d8a51b8ca2bc4b94e05b4a9e8c301.abstract: <jats:p>In this chapter, we explore the process of achieving supply chain resilience in Industrial Metaverse environments by embedding digital twin technology and blockchain-based distributed trust mechanisms. No single technology is sufficient to address the triple crises of disruption, opacity, and accountability in contemporary supply chains. The chapter makes its case through trans-disciplinary scholarship spanning supply chain management, digital transformation, blockchain governance, and Industry 4.0. They introduce a 5-layer conceptual framework to illustrate how these physical operations, data connectivity, simulation, distributed verification, and governance layers are interdependent among each other via the Digital Twin–Blockchain Trust Framework, which allows us to visualize how such Human-centric smart systems can lead towards Visibility, Traceability, and Adaptive Resilience eventually. Investigates sustainability implications, ethical risks, and cyber vulnerabilities, as well as concrete pathways for managerial adoption.</jats:p>

title: A Framework for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Supply-Chain Optimization (HQCSCO)
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

d1b522f79a68031ab548219a1152e6dfcb83f336.abstract: <jats:p>The study presents the earliest effort to conceptualize SCM integration with quantum computing principles, providing dynamic capabilities for SCM. It proposes a unique interdisciplinary framework that demonstrates where hybrid quantum-classical approaches can realise value, and specifies the conditions that organizations must meet to adopt such methods. In this article, a conceptual framework has been proposed for HQCSCO. This framework facilitates key decision-making areas such as inventory optimisation, production scheduling, and logistics routing, where quantum-enhanced algorithms could supplement classical models to enhance performance. At the managerial level, the framework helps manufacturing leaders to determine viability, prioritize high-impact use cases, and develop future-ready digital capabilities that enhance cost efficiency, agility, and resilience. The research provides a conceptually-based baseline of quantum-facile supply chains and offers a research agenda to investigate the strategic, ethical, and operational implications thereof.</jats:p>

title: Immersive Stock Control for Virtual Depots via Process Digital Twins and Topological Data Analysis
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
181d6ce5803b6924cc02dfd46f21bf24456d4579.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter presents the development of an advanced inventory management model for virtual warehouses. By combining process digital twins with Topological Data Analysis, this model strives to support supervisors in pinpointing bottleneck formations that standard performance indicators are unable to reveal. The methodology describes how IoT-like intralogistics events are interpreted as augmented point clouds. The methodology also describes how persistent homology is computed through Vietoris-Rips and Alpha-complex filtrations, and how topological indicators are transformed into an immersive decision layer through the framework's comprehensive approach to bottleneck and Wasserstein distances. The computational case interprets fragmentation, routing loops, and volumetric cavities as congestion, vulnerability, and latent capacity indicators. The results show how the persistent topology of the model offers a candidate articulate layer for the process digital twins. The model still needs additional empirical calibration, for operational interventions in a physical warehouse.</jats:p>

title: Artificial Intelligence in Smart Ports and Sustainable Maritime Logistics
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
fb27937fd6ed5b67a638e8b71b2617dfc041ff66.abstract: <jats:p>Artificial intelligence is transforming maritime logistics by improving operational efficiency, sustainability, and digital integration. At the same time, the Industrial Metaverse is reshaping supply chain management through real time data, digital twins, and intelligent decision environments. However, the linkage between these developments remains underexplored. This study conducts a bibliometric and thematic review of 208 Scopus indexed journal articles published between 2013 and 2025 using VOSviewer and Bibliometrix. The analysis identifies key trends and four thematic clusters: smart ports, green shipping, digital transformation, and governance. Findings indicate that existing research is technologically advanced but fragmented, with limited focus on system integration, human interaction, and economic feasibility. The study highlights critical gaps and provides insights for advancing next generation, Industrial Metaverse based maritime supply chains.</jats:p>

title: Challenges of Industry 4.0 Adoption in Malaysia's Ship Repair Industry
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
a5c2578bb1ed98f301ea6bb9016c9962fd028ba1.abstract: <jats:p>The adoption of Industrial Revolution 4.0 (IR 4.0) technologies in Malaysia's ship repair industry presents significant opportunities to enhance operational efficiency, safety, and global competitiveness. However, the transition toward digital transformation remains constrained by multiple structural, technological, and organizational challenges. This study aims to identify and analyze the key barriers to IR 4.0 adoption using a mixed-method approach that integrates literature review and empirical data collected from 175 industry experts. The findings reveal five critical challenges, namely technological infrastructure and investment, data management and integration, workforce skills, cybersecurity, and regulatory frameworks. Among these, infrastructure and data-related challenges emerged as the most significant. The findings contribute to both academic literature and industry practice by offering a comprehensive understanding of IR 4.0 adoption in a developing maritime context.</jats:p>

title: Industrial Metaverse and AI-Driven Food Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
47d3e0515c13fda1af2da5950b7c6fa396315d15.abstract: <jats:p>This study explores how agriculture and food logistics are being transformed through artificial intelligence and Industrial Metaverse-enabled supply chain systems in emerging economies. It examines the shift from traditional linear food systems toward immersive, data-driven, and phygital ecosystems integrating digital twins, blockchain, IoT, and AR/VR technologies. Using a qualitative multiple-case study approach, the research analyzes India, China, Brazil, and Russia to understand how policy reforms, technological adoption, and infrastructure development influence food security and resilience. Findings show that AI-enabled forecasting, real-time monitoring, and immersive simulation improve supply chain efficiency, reduce food waste, and enhance sustainability. However, challenges such as infrastructure gaps, digital inequality, and limited workforce readiness persist. The study emphasizes the importance of integrated policy frameworks and education systems to enable next-generation resilient food supply chains.</jats:p>

title: Sustainability and the Circular Economy in Virtualized Settings
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
ebe6f0b34ee1b19fb405906ddf6f10d2270baad4.abstract: <jats:p>Supply chains are under mounting pressure to reconcile operational performance with environmental responsibility — a tension that conventional efficiency tools and isolated green initiatives have not resolved satisfactorily. This chapter examines how the industrial metaverse, as an integrative platform encompassing digital twins, extended reality interfaces, and AI-enabled analytics, can embed circular economy principles within supply chains. Drawing on recent scholarship, it traces alignment between closed-loop material flows and the informational closure enabled by metaverse environments. Attention is given to enabling conditions and persistent barriers — organisational, technological, and regulatory — shaping adoption. The chapter situates these developments within the digital economy, considering how financial digitalization and platform economics affect viability, and offers practical guidance followed by a research agenda.</jats:p>

title: Energy Paradox
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
5978dd6e52239fe81f0eae8216a3d68a87b18554.abstract: <jats:p>The consequence of Carbon Savings (CS) on green energy cost reduction (GECR) using Biogas Logistics Optimization (BGLO) in Tanzania is analysed in this work. The quantitative research approach was adopted with 280 respondents of biogas and energy sector. The results indicate that, the CS has a significant satisfactory impact on GECR and BGLO. Moreover, the cost reduction effect of BGLO is meaningfully mediated, works across CS and cost efficiency. The findings reveal that benefits of environmental sustainability depend not just on the environmental sustainability, but also on the efficiency of logistic systems. The study combines both the SCMT and EET to enunciate the relationships. The results suggest from a practical point of view that the performance of biogas systems could be further enhanced by improving the efficiency of logistics infrastructure and logistics coordination. The study provides valuable policy guidance and insights for future research.</jats:p>

title: Ethical Governance and Cybersecurity Frameworks for Decentralized Immersive Supply Chains in the Industrial Metaverse
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
b543d24b4de0e90e3100ab0ae1c6f35a85be60f6.abstract: <jats:p>The Industrial Metaverse is transforming supply chain management by creating persistent, immersive, and decentralized virtual environments where stakeholders collaborate through digital twins, smart contracts, and spatial computing. This shift introduces ethical and cybersecurity challenges threatening trust, transparency, and resilience. This chapter examines governance and security risks in operating supply chains within shared virtual spaces, addressing three pillars: data sovereignty and intellectual property protection, ethical algorithmic design for automated procurement, and privacy-preserving verification including zero-knowledge proofs. The chapter makes three contributions: it applies the “Decentralization Paradox” to supply chain governance, proposes a Hybrid Governance Framework integrating protocol-level, organizational, and regulatory mechanisms, and develops a Risk Severity Index for threat prioritization. These provide a foundational governance architecture for next-generation supply chain operations.</jats:p>

title: The Decentralization Paradox
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
2d9915accb591108b34ff431c8da88d1f6ef5a75.abstract: <jats:p>Industrial metaverse supply chain ecosystems present a dichotomy: the decentralized nature of blockchain governance versus the centralized character of organizational control. This chapter discusses this decentralization dilemma and develops a hybrid governance model combining the two. Methodologically, the study draws on Institutional Theory and Transaction Cost Economics, and by combining literature on blockchain governance, metaverse adoption, and supply chain coordination, develops hypotheses for further testing. The results indicate that neither entirely decentralized nor completely centralized mechanisms satisfy the requirements of metaverse-enabled supply chains. The suggested model uses blockchain to ensure transaction trust while leaving strategy-making to centralized authorities. This is the first study offering a theoretical explanation of how both governance modes can coexist in immersive industrial environments, filling the identified research gap. The framework is conceptual and needs empirical testing through manufacturing and logistics cases.</jats:p>

title: Metaverse-Enabled Leadership for Industrial Supply Chains
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
655782e4fe7f1ef790e19e8011646a5a0b9572a9.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid evolution of digital technologies, including digital twins, blockchain, and the Industrial Metaverse, is transforming global supply chains from linear systems into interconnected, data-driven ecosystems. This study examines how immersive metaverse environments reshape leadership practices within supply chains, emphasizing adaptive, collaborative, and inclusive behaviors. Through avatar-mediated interactions, gamification, and virtual prototyping, leaders engage in realistic simulations, enhancing decision-making, coordination, and stakeholder engagement across distributed operations. While immersive technologies offer experiential learning and operational resilience, challenges such as cognitive overload, limited nonverbal cues, and unequal access highlight the need for context-sensitive strategies. A conceptual framework is proposed linking technological affordances, leadership behaviors, and supply chain outcomes, providing a foundation for research and practical guidance on metaverse-enabled leadership in complex industrial networks.</jats:p>

title: Governance and Metaverse Leadership in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Next-Generation Supply Chain Management in the Industrial Metaverse
38378b71005194bfbcd5ca78001d409d20c03788.abstract: <jats:p>This study develops a comprehensive conceptual–operational framework for governance and leadership in Metaverse-enabled higher education. Grounded in digital transformation, leadership theory, and immersive technologies, the framework integrates five interdependent layers: governance, leadership, technology, operations, and evaluation. It emphasizes hybrid governance, adaptive and distributed leadership, secure and scalable technologies, and operational alignment, while addressing ethical considerations such as data privacy, equity, and algorithmic fairness. By linking theory with practice, the framework provides higher education institutions with guidance for effective, sustainable, and inclusive implementation of immersive academic ecosystems, supporting continuous evaluation, strategic decision-making, and organizational learning. The study contributes to both scholarly understanding and practical pathways for navigating hybrid virtual and physical academic environments.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
Beyond Recognition
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
8d55c03606f397dfebd690ec5704784da2344f3c.abstract: <jats:p>Current e-learning systems are still not well-suited to learn in real-time as individuals' emotional and cognitive state. The chapter presents AIALE (Affective Intelligence Adaptive Learning Engine), a multimodal system capable of embedding facial coding, bio signals, keystroke dynamics and eye-tracking in a single pipeline and with sub-500ms inference latency. The AIALE's three-tier architecture consists of a deep learning-based effect inference, a reinforcement learning-based curriculum control and a pedagogic intervention broker. AIALE was tested with 214 university students from four disciplines and led to statistically significant increases in knowledge gain (31% above that of a knowledge-adaptive baseline) as well as to an increase in engagement duration and a balance of cognitive load, compared to a knowledge-adaptive baseline and a non-adaptive control. An ablation analysis shows that the most significant affective dimensions for adaptive interventions' quality are confusion and cognitive load detection. The chapter also introduces five research gaps and explores emerging research avenues such as generative AI tutoring agents and explainable affective adaptation.</jats:p>

title: Camera-Based Deep Learning Framework for Real-Time Emotion-Aware Engagement Detection in E-Learning
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
10cfc4979912c42a01924f13bd2193ca5e197ab1.abstract: <jats:p>The explosive expansion of digital learning platforms has revolutionized the manner in which students access, consume, and interact with academic content. Sustaining high levels of engagement within online spaces, though, remains perhaps the most critical challenge facing higher education. Conventional methods of measuring engagement—e.g., tracking presence, post-session questionnaires, or physiological sensors—are intrusively burdensome, not very reliable, and less than ideal for widespread implementation. Technological developments in artificial intelligence (AI) and deep learning provide non-invasive means, notably via camera-based emotion detection systems that are able to track and decipher learner engagement real-time. This chapter suggests a human-focused deep learning approach that incorporates facial emotion detection with adaptive learning routes to boost learner engagement and mental growth in e-learning contexts.</jats:p>

title: Challenges and Ethical Considerations in Gamified and Cognitive Learning in Cybersecurity Education
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
fe7c56a27e63d56369910ade1fabf1dae4d33295.abstract: <jats:p>Gamified and cognitive learning in cybersecurity education is gaining popularity, but it brings its own set of challenges, particularly when it comes to ethics. Training through games can sharpen technical skills, yet there's always the risk of blurring the lines between ethical hacking and actual cybercrime. Some learners may be tempted to misuse their knowledge, especially if ethical considerations aren't woven into the experience from the start. Then there's the question of real-world readiness—does solving puzzles in a simulated environment translate to handling live cyber threats? Beyond that, data privacy is a concern. Gamified platforms track progress, but how much of that data should they collect, and who gets access? And let's not ignore the psychology behind game mechanics, does intense competition fuel motivation or push players toward reckless behavior? The key lies in balance. Industry and academia need to step in with clear ethical guidelines, ensuring that gamification encourages responsibility alongside skill-building. A well-designed system can use storytelling, role-playing, and collaborative challenges to reinforce ethical decision-making rather than just technical mastery. AI could play a role in adapting training to individuals, but it raises ethical dilemmas. Cybersecurity threats are constantly changing, so training must evolve too. Gamified education can be a powerful tool, but only if it's designed with ethics at its core.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning Architectures for Real-Time Emotion and Engagement Detection in E-Learning Platforms
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
f9731fd32e93095cf320cc72899c5ae1486d338c.abstract: <jats:p>The integration of deep learning into e-learning environments has revolutionised the way learners interact with educational content. This study explores the design and implementation of deep learning architectures for real-time emotion and engagement detection in e-learning platforms. By leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNNs), recurrent neural networks (RNNs), and transformer-based models, the proposed framework captures multimodal data such as facial expressions, speech tone, eye movement, and physiological signals to assess learners' emotional states and engagement levels dynamically. The system provides adaptive feedback to instructors and personalised interventions to learners, enhancing cognitive growth and overall learning outcomes. The research also discusses the challenges of real-time processing, model interpretability, data privacy, and ethical considerations associated with emotion recognition technologies in education.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning for Modern E-Learning Systems
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
9aaf4dfff445fa1aad16b80d1c5376fcd12ec6c4.abstract: <jats:p>Models that learn from users and content interact at scale. This chapter articulates the many uses of highly layered neural networks in personalization, applied feedback, and text, speech, code, image, and video assistance. The main model families are described: CNNs, RNNs / LSTMs, transformers, autoencoders, and other generative models; as are the approaches to training, optimizing, regularizing, and deploying models. Representation learning from unstructured data, adaptive pathways, engagement and emotion detection, and predicting performance and studying are learning outcomes that guide model choice. System elements include data gathering, analytics, model serving in-cloud or on-device, and scale. Intelligent tutoring, recommendation, auto-grading, and dialogue systems on modern platforms are current use cases. Trade-offs include privacy, sparse supervision, bias, lack of explainability, seamlessness to legacy systems, and computation cost. Real-world deployments, both successful and not, are the focus of the illustrative case studies. The chapter's focus is on core techniques and design choices to build the next generation of e-learning systems.</jats:p>

title: Deep Learning-Driven Emotion Recognition for Personalized and Adaptive E-Learning Systems
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
ce676f08ce46956bb22f53f59a27b6cbe5ec864b.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter explores how deep learning–based emotion recognition enhances student engagement and cognitive growth in e-learning environments. By leveraging CNN and LSTM architectures, the proposed framework detects learners' emotions from facial and behavioral cues in real time, enabling adaptive instructional responses. Through camera-based, non-invasive monitoring, emotions such as confusion, curiosity, or satisfaction are quantified to personalize learning experiences and improve retention. The chapter also discusses dataset selection, model design, and integration into Learning Management Systems (LMS). Case insights demonstrate how emotion-aware systems foster empathy, motivation, and inclusivity in digital education. Ethical considerations privacy, fairness, and explainability are addressed to ensure responsible AI deployment. The study establishes emotion recognition as a cornerstone for intelligent, adaptive, and human-centered e-learning ecosystems that align technology with emotional intelligence and pedagogical effectiveness.</jats:p>

title: How Gamification Mechanics Improve Cybersecurity Learning Retention
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
e507f4e7f41e686a6ea10856a0a000bbacf36594.abstract: <jats:p>Gamification taps into how the brain processes rewards, emotions, and repetition, making it a powerful tool for cybersecurity education. When learners engage with challenges that trigger dopamine release—like solving puzzles, earning achievements, or progressing through a story—retention improves. The way emotions shape memory also plays a role; high-stakes simulations and immersive storytelling make security concepts stick. Incorporating game mechanics, such as real-time feedback, narrative-driven exercises, and adaptive difficulty, strengthens learning. Capture the Flag competitions and VR-based training reinforce hands-on skills, while spaced repetition counters memory decay. More than just engagement, this approach helps reduce anxiety by creating a safe space for trial and error, building confidence without the fear of real-world consequences. As AI begins to refine personalized learning paths, cybersecurity training can adapt to individual strengths and weaknesses. Long-term, this shift could shape a more prepared, responsive workforce—one that learns through experience, not just theory. But with any gamified system, balance is key.</jats:p>

title: Natural Language Processing for Interactive Learning Experiences
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
987c3de7f795db1cc232a6a4b1b49390a428ce0f.abstract: <jats:p>Natural Language Processing (NLP) has become a core component for next generation e-learning ecosystems, especially in content delivery. It enables platforms to understand, respond and adapt to individual learners. With the rise of deep learning models especially transformer based architectures, NLP now offers state of the art capabilities for real-time interaction, personalized feedback, and adaptive learning pathways. This chapter examines NLP-driven systems powered by deep learning to enhance learner engagement, motivation, and cognitive development. It is developed by converting static educational materials into dynamic, conversational, and highly interactive experiences. The key ideas in this chapter includes understanding text, language models that can generate responses, intelligent tutoring systems, automatic grading, feedback that considers emotions, and learning that uses multiple types of media (such as text, audio, and images). Practical use cases and emerging research trends are highlighted. Ethical, pedagogical and technological challenges are also discussed.</jats:p>

title: Passive Learning to Active Engagement
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
eacaa5f4ae36bc7dc2909810ec0a52e6a7081ebd.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid evolution of digital technologies has transformed the educational landscape, challenging traditional passive learning models and emphasizing the need for active engagement in deep learning. Passive learning, characterized by one-way information delivery and limited learner interaction, often results in superficial comprehension and low retention. In contrast, active engagement leverages interactive digital tools, collaborative strategies, and learner-centered approaches to foster critical thinking, problem-solving, and meaningful knowledge construction. This chapter explores the theoretical underpinnings of passive and active learning, examines the pedagogical shift facilitated by digital technologies, and highlights effective strategies for promoting deep learning in contemporary educational environments. Case studies from diverse educational contexts illustrate how digital pedagogy can bridge the gap between passive reception and active participation, ultimately enhancing learner motivation, engagement, and long-term retention.</jats:p>

title: Real-Time Multimodal Engagement Detection in E-Learning
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
cc8c8875c98107da22dfb5309173f1535042c386.abstract: <jats:p>The transition from in-person classrooms to digital and hybrid modes of learning has created new opportunities but has also posed several serious problems for education. One of the most key problems is the measurement of student engagement. This chapter discusses the use of deep learning for multimodal engagement detection to analyze visual data, auditory data, and behavioral data. By combining these signals, the adaptive feedback loops can be built supporting the learning. This chapter presents artificial intelligence together with psychological theories of the motivation, attention, and cognitive load in order to design human-centered environments that help teachers to be more efficient. Ethical issues like privacy, consent, and bias are dealt with to make sure they are utilized in a responsible manner. The chapter includes case studies from India and also other parts of the globe, showing the opportunities and challenges. The design of the system is proposed as a framework including pipelines, and integration with learning platforms.</jats:p>

title: The Psychology of Deep Learning for Student Engagement and Cognitive Development
container-title: Deep Learning for Engagement and Cognitive Growth in E-Learning
388c0f1038cc6f8828ff44b71c150147ada103bd.abstract: <jats:p>Against the background of deep learning for engagement and cognitive growth in e-learning, the purpose of this chapter is to discuss findings from a real-world case study implementation at a Higher Education Institution (HEI) in Namibia. Towards addressing the psychology of deep learning for student engagement and cognitive development by reconfiguring e-learning accessibility via mobile technologies, the main focus of the chapter will be on tools, platforms, and gaps, as well as challenges and limitations, related to e-learning ecosystems. Future research directions based on the findings will be presented in order to come to conclusions toward smarter, fairer, human-centered learning.</jats:p>

666d4eec1099228678f9ba6af74a13a32a982a4f.abstract: <jats:p>The growing complexity of higher education administration has exposed the limitations of fragmented, rule-based systems that struggle to support timely and data-driven decision-making. This chapter examines agentic artificial intelligence (AI) as a catalyst for transforming administrative ecosystems into adaptive, intelligent, and coordinated systems. Moving beyond traditional automation, agentic AI introduces autonomy, context-awareness, and continuous learning, enabling real-time data integration, predictive–prescriptive analytics, and workflow orchestration across core domains. Drawing on frameworks such as multi-agent systems, decision intelligence, and socio-technical systems, the chapter analyzes how agentic AI reshapes institutional processes and decision structures. It also highlights key challenges, including data silos, governance complexities, and ethical concerns. Ultimately, the chapter argues that effective implementation requires systemic integration, robust governance, and strong human–AI collaboration.</jats:p>

title: Agentic Artificial Intelligence for Decision-Making Augmentation in Higher Education Administration
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
4753ec1853130197948d90a206fa4f559f31bc1c.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid digital transformation of higher education has intensified the need for more adaptive, data-driven administrative decision-making systems. This chapter examines the emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) as a transformative approach that extends beyond traditional analytics and generative models by enabling autonomous, goal-directed, and context-aware decision processes. It outlines the conceptual foundations of agentic AI through intelligent agent theory, decision intelligence, and socio-technical systems, and analyzes its core capabilities, including perception, reasoning, planning, and action. The chapter further explores its applications across key administrative domains and highlights its potential to enhance efficiency, predictive capacity, and institutional responsiveness. Despite these benefits, critical challenges related to governance, ethics, data fragmentation, and human-AI collaboration are emphasized, underscoring the need for balanced and responsible implementation.</jats:p>

title: Decision Intelligence for AI-Enabled University Governance and Data-Driven Administrative Transformation
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
1ea21bd12f81b110514bb8aff08dc36ff1204ee4.abstract: <jats:p>The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming governance and administrative processes in higher education institutions. Traditional systems relying on manual operations and fragmented data are increasingly inadequate. This chapter proposes an AI-driven decision intelligence framework for efficient, data-driven, and policy-aligned governance. The framework integrates data collection, preprocessing, feature selection, and predictive analytics within a unified architecture, where institutional data from student, financial, and human resource systems are analyzed using machine learning models to generate insights. These are refined through policy-based decision mechanisms to ensure transparency and compliance. Results show improved decision accuracy, operational efficiency, and reduced processing time, supported by dashboards for real-time monitoring. Ethical concerns such as data privacy and bias are also addressed. A case study from Tamil Nadu demonstrates the framework's applicability as a scalable model for AI-enabled governance.</jats:p>

title: Agentic AI as a Governance Partner in Higher Education Leadership
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
57435d97d2fd69fae64c511686c94b37c80641ef.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter advances the argument that agentic artificial intelligence should be theorized as a governance partner in higher education leadership rather than as a mere administrative tool. As universities operate within intensifying accountability, datafication, and audit regimes, agentic systems increasingly participate in enrollment, budgeting, accreditation, and research decisions, reshaping institutional decision architectures. To address this shift, this chapter proposes the Strategic Agentic Governance Framework, a feedback-driven model linking data intelligence, normative framing, decision orchestration, accountability, and adaptive institutional learning. Drawing on distributed leadership, institutional agency, algorithmic governance, and socio-technical systems theory, the framework reconceptualizes leadership as meta-governance, the deliberate design of hybrid human and machine decision systems. The chapter also examines accountability diffusion, algorithmic bias, and data sovereignty, and offers testable propositions and a maturity continuum for future research.</jats:p>

title: Digital Catalytic Leadership for Governing Agentic AI
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics
Agentic AI for Transforming Higher Education Administration Systems
a7a2f25db22c009ea70fb3c60ff8c7c5966288e7.abstract: <jats:p>The evolution of agentic AI is transforming higher education administration beyond simple automation. This chapter examines the governance challenges of AI integration in universities and proposes Digital Catalytic Leadership (DCL) as an adaptive governance framework. The study finds that while agentic AI can improve administrative effectiveness, it also creates challenges related to accountability, data security, and human–AI relations. This chapter argues that DCL is important for building adaptive, ethical, and human-centered higher education governance in the AI era.</jats:p>

title: From Paperwork to Predictive Governance
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

59ed15c0f7f338ea6f034d707cac8523fbdf31f4.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter presents a Cambodia-specific framework for implementing agentic AI in higher education administration, converting bureaucracy and paperwork into a predictive, evidence-based governance model. Cambodia's higher education faces accountability, accreditation, student expectations, and limited admin capacity. AI adoption is fragmented, causing delays, duplicate reports, and inconsistent services. The chapter suggests agentic AI can act as an orchestration layer for institutions by integrating systems and enhancing decision-making in Admissions, Enrolment, Scheduling, Finance, HR, Research Administration, and Quality Assurance. It highlights key use cases such as coordinating student services, automating accreditation evidence management, forecasting queues, and identifying compliance gaps. The chapter aims to provide a pragmatic policy synthesis based on practice and resource constraints in Cambodia. The chapter's main contribution is a practical model to facilitate the adoption of responsible agentic AI that aims to improve administrative efficiency and transparency.</jats:p>

title: Intelligent Budget Allocation and Predictive Financial Analytics Using AI in Higher Education
container-title: Advances in Computational Intelligence and Robotics

811b776505e2e740c926ee67de48c35b2159227e.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter considers the potential use of an agentic AI in changing the face of financial planning and budgeting in higher education organizations characterized by uncertain funding, unpredictable enrollments, and increasing accountability. This chapter criticizes the conventional approach to incremental budgeting and advances a governance-centered model in which AI functions as an agent for enhancing collaboration in financial decision-making rather than taking control from people's hands. Informed by Dynamic Capabilities theory, the contribution illustrates the role of AI in improving the capabilities for sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring at institutions for adaptive management. This chapter further develops the concept of a four-step RACT model for implementing AI in responsible ways. The contribution is enriched through institutional case illustrations with emphasis on the advantages gained through AI adoption. The challenges associated with the application of AI in financial management are discussed, alongside mitigation approaches. Research gaps are clearly stated.</jats:p>

c1ad93ee7e0991c260ac643de8c3fa1e55541ddd.abstract: <jats:p>The appearance of Agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Indian academic spaces has ushered in a wave of revolutionary changes, bringing new tools like intelligent automation, supporting governance, intelligent data-based decisions, and the like. This subchapter attempts to bring out a framework, A3 Model, where Agentic AI, Administrative Resilience, and Educational Excellence are offered within one overarching design from a more applied framework. The chapter goes on with an empirical inquiry where mixed methods and PLS-SEM are used on data from Indian universities, focusing on how Agentic AI shapes institutional responsiveness and academic performance. The results show that there exists a strong and positive connection among the capabilities of AI, the existence of an agile organization, and the realization of desirable academic outcomes, but most significantly, the interaction of those effects in the context of escalating and fostering the productive and efficient administration within the higher education system.</jats:p>

title: Administrative System Transformation Through Agentic AI in Enrollment and Admissions Management

19d4c9a3cbac21418f82ad721e79494df8fa79eb.abstract: <jats:p>Administrative challenges are increasing in higher education establishments in light of the rising enrollment pressures, changing student needs, and heightened demands for accountability. Agentic AI, with its capacity to self-directly perceive, plan, act, and learn, opens up avenues for a novel way to revolutionize enrollment and admissions management. This chapter provides an overview of the ways in which agentic AI is transforming the enrollment cycle, including the engagement of students, admission applications, prediction and planning, decision-making, and yield management. Based on the recent research and practical experience of various educational establishments, the potential, as well as possible difficulties associated with automation, ethical issues, privacy concerns, workforce transformation, among other issues, are discussed.</jats:p>

00d998159a5393674028a10b076cd1fb8a858ea4.abstract: <jats:p>This chapter examines the role of agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) in transforming enrollment and admissions management within higher education institutions. The chapter discusses the evolution of admissions systems from traditional manual structures to intelligent, data-driven administrative ecosystems supported by predictive analytics, workflow automation, applicant screening, and conversational AI. The study highlights how AI-enabled systems improve enrollment forecasting, communication responsiveness, institutional coordination, and operational efficiency while reducing administrative delays and inconsistencies. Empirical findings from multi-institutional analysis demonstrate measurable improvements in applicant engagement, screening accuracy, workflow synchronization, and fairness in admissions processes. The chapter further explores governance, ethical considerations, explainability, and human-AI collaboration frameworks necessary for responsible implementation of intelligent admissions systems in higher education.</jats:p>

title: Design and Validation of a Novel Planar 2R1T Remote Center-of-Motion Mechanism Composing of Dual-Triangular and Straight-Line Linkages
container-title: Journal of Mechanisms and Robotics
caf43fb798aa694f48d6f5c32707dcb9a24ad400.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>Benefiting from small incision and fast recovery, minimally invasive surgeries (MIS) exhibit great advantages in clinical operations. In such kind of surgeries, the remote center-of-motion (RCM) mechanisms play an important role owing to their special motion characteristics. This paper presents the design of a novel planar RCM mechanism of two rotational and one translational degrees-of-freedom (DOF). In the proposed design, the mobility of RCM mechanism is decomposed into one-DOF pure rotation and translation with a remote stationary point. The dual-triangular linkage and the Peaucellier–Lipkin straight-line linkage are introduced to achieve the remote rotation and translation, respectively. Inspired by the concept of virtual screw, a dual-helical differential-motion joint is particularly designed to generate the coaxial rotation and translation. A preliminary prototype is developed to validate the feasibility of the designed RCM mechanism. The experimental results show that the developed prototype is easy to control and of acceptable positioning accuracy, which manifests potential application in MIS.</jats:p>

title: Assessing the Quality of AI Explanations of Atrial Fibrillation: Comparative Analysis of ChatGPT and Google Gemini
container-title: JMIR Formative Research
598e2fa6d5c1d1ee8bb1eebc101a66353744cb13.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Atrial fibrillation (AF) is one of the most common arrhythmias and is associated with multiple risk factors, including stroke and heart failure. Therefore, it is important that accurate and comprehensive educational resources on AF are available. Artificial intelligence (AI) platforms such as Google Gemini and ChatGPT are emerging tools for medical education. To our knowledge, this is the first study to assess the quality of these platforms for AF education.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Objective</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>This pilot study aimed to (1) assess the quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini explanations of AF and its treatment, (2) compare responses from both platforms, and (3) analyze differences in interpretation between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The prompt “Explain atrial fibrillation and how to treat it to a patient” was entered into both ChatGPT and Google Gemini. The responses, along with a survey created in Google Forms, were sent out to potential participants between September and October 2024. The survey questions were derived from the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool for Printable Materials and DISCERN criteria. Each survey question was multiple choice and rated on a 5-point Likert scale, where 1 indicated strong disagreement and 5 indicated strong agreement. Averages of each answer from the survey were calculated and compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The survey was completed by 28 participants, including cardiologists and cardiology fellows and 17 nonmedical professionals (college graduates not employed in the medical field). No significant overall quality differences were observed between ChatGPT and Google Gemini. When comparing participant groups, cardiologists rated AI-generated responses higher than nonmedical professionals for perceived bias (mean 3.82 vs mean 4.33; P=.04) and for explaining consequences of no treatment (mean 2.85 vs mean 1.86; P=.005). In contrast, nonmedical professionals rated structural and organizational features more favorably than cardiologists, including visual cues (mean 3.97 vs mean 2.48; P<.001), informative headers (mean 4.77 vs mean 3.95; P=.001), concise sections (mean 4.71 vs mean 4.29; P=.04), identifiable patient actions (mean 4.21 vs mean 3.19; P=.04), and references to additional resources (mean 2.65 vs mean 1.71; P=.006).</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>The comparable quality of ChatGPT and Google Gemini suggests that both are viable for AF education. Differences in ratings of organizational features versus perceptions of bias and consequences of no treatment highlight a disconnect between cardiologists and nonmedical professionals. To optimize clinical application, cardiologists should evaluate both comprehensiveness and clarity of AI-generated responses. This serves as a pilot study, and future research should focus on longitudinal studies of AI-generated responses and their effects on clinical outcomes.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>

title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
container-title: eLife
42e0bff514a13e990dde6d5376170bcb87804ae4.abstract: <jats:p>The visual system can flexibly adjust attentional deployment to match task demands, but whether observers can proactively modulate the spatial scope of attention based on expectations about upcoming search difficulty remains unclear. According to the zoom lens model, attention can narrow or broaden its spatial extent, with narrower focus enhancing processing efficiency, a mechanism that would benefit target discrimination in crowded displays. We tested whether observers adjust attentional scope when expecting sparse versus dense search arrays by combining spatial cueing with block-wise manipulations of display density expectations. Participants performed a visual search task in which endogenous cues predicted target location, while blocks predominantly contained either sparse (1 target, 3 distractors) or dense (1 target, 7 distractors) displays. We applied inverted encoding models to broadband EEG data to reconstruct spatial channel tuning functions, enabling precise characterization of both the locus and breadth of attentional deployment. Behaviorally, expecting difficult searches selectively improved accuracy at cued locations without costs elsewhere. Consistent with this selective benefit, neural measurements revealed that expectancy enhanced the amplitude of spatially selective responses at the attended location but did not alter tuning width. These findings demonstrate that expectations about search difficulty modulate attention through gain-based signal enhancement rather than adjustments to spatial scope, revealing that preparatory attentional control operates via amplitude modulation within a stable spatial focus. This mechanism complements reactive attentional adjustments and provides an efficient means for the visual system to optimize processing under predictable task demands.</jats:p>

<jats:p>This research presents the results of a systematic review that analyses the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, social-emotional skills and self-esteem in students enrolled in sports programmes in Colombia, with the aim of identifying the factors that influence their positive attitude towards entrepreneurial capacity. In the literature review, 100 articles and academic research papers were selected between 2019 and 2025, prioritised from 42,958 results from different resources such as reference databases, multidisciplinary databases, academic repositories and academic journals. The databases with the highest number of results were Scopus, Web of Science, Wiley, Springer Nature, Science Direct, Ebsco Host, among others such as (COnnecting REpositories), Taylor & Francis, and Google Scholar. The results showed an interest in academia to research and reflect on the relationship between entrepreneurial culture, emotional skills, and young people. However, in most studies, entrepreneurial culture is associated with variables such as emotional intelligence and social skills in university contexts, leaving the field of the relationship between these variables and the field of sports somewhat lacking in studies. Studies that explore this relationship in depth conclude that athletes develop socio-emotional skills that make them strong candidates for entrepreneurship. However, there are limitations in the implementation of mechanisms that promote an entrepreneurial culture ( ) in university contexts for young people studying sports programmes.

title: VHMP: A High-efficacy and Parallel Processing Approach for CGRCA Supporting Virtual Heterogeneous Multi-core and Intra-core Multitask Pipeline
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
6069641410fbf34886a36b583f52e136660d22c8.abstract: <jats:p>The performance enhancements of coarse-grain reconfigurable cryptographic arrays (CGRCAs) through technology upgrades and increasing chip size are approaching limits. Enhancing parallel processing capabilities can relieve the computational burden on CGRCA in high-density computing scenarios. Specifically, a novel parallel processing approach is introduced in this article, named virtual heterogeneous multi-core pipelining (VHMP). VHMP supports virtual heterogeneous multi-core and intra-core multitask pipelining. Informed by hardware virtualization principles and analysis of CGRCA architectures, VHMP constructs virtual computing cores (VCCs) on CGRCA using multi-launch pipelines and implements multitask interleave pipelines within each VCC, enabling parallel processing at pipeline, task, and instruction levels. Furthermore, a hierarchical control mechanism is embedded within VHMP, integrating virtual computing path level and task-level management. This control mechanism allows diverse cryptographic algorithms to run concurrently without being bound to specific types or modes. Finally, applying VHMP to a 32 × 4 CGRCA, 32 heterogeneous VCCs are instantiated, with each core handling up to 16 interleaved tasks. Compared to treating CGRCA as a homogeneous multi-core processor, the VHMP approach achieves an average acceleration of 4.33 × (up to 6.34 ×) with quadrupled instruction execution capability. Additionally, the control mechanism reduces context volume to 18.7% and boosts configuration speed by 3 ×. Compared with related architectures, VHMP improves CGRCA throughput by an average of 5.3 ×.</jats:p>

title: Graphene-Based Interconnect Exploration for FPGA Design and Optimization Towards the End of the Roadmap

e4661457e8c7a67399488d41681b0b4a0b41cb22.abstract: <jats:p>The emerging graphene interconnect technology is expected to be a promising alternative to traditional interconnect technologies due to its superior conductivity. Because of the dominant impact of global routing on the overall performance of a widely used application, the Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), this work investigates the potential advantage of using graphene-based interconnects to replace conventional copper (Cu) for global routing. Furthermore, a scalability analysis is performed, and the effects of technology node scaling from 7 nm to 1.5 nm are evaluated using lateral gate-all-around field-effect transistors (LGAAFETs) within the proposed system-technology co-design (STCO) framework. Key material-level parameters, including the mean free path (MFP), contact resistance, and the number of graphene layers, are systematically analyzed. Benchmark simulations demonstrate that a 32% improvement in the energy-delay product (EDP) is achieved with graphene-based interconnects compared to Cu counterparts at the 7 nm technology node, and an additional 46% reduction is observed at the 1.5 nm technology node. It is important to note that this work is an exploratory STCO study incorporating cross-layer design considerations, with a focus on long-term trends rather than short-term manufacturability.</jats:p>

title: LASM: Extensible Competitive Scheduling Framework for VLIW Assembly Optimization
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
d1804df4679dc580d7bd65e32240c18e9cb9fc7f.abstract: <jats:p>Very Long Instruction Word (VLIW) architectures deliver compelling performance-energy-cost advantages for automotive, AI, and high-performance computing. However, a persistent performance-productivity gap limits broader adoption: manual assembly optimization achieves superior performance but requires substantial expertise, while automated compilation underperforms. Existing assembly-level optimization tools commit to single scheduling strategies, unable to adapt to diverse program patterns. This article presents LASM, the first symbolic assembly framework enabling competitive multi-strategy orchestration for complete VLIW programs. Rather than committing to a single algorithm, multiple scheduling strategies simultaneously optimize identical code regions, with the framework automatically selecting the top solution through feasibility-driven ranking. LASM features standardized extension interfaces enabling plugin-style strategy integration and unified scheduling primitives eliminating algorithmic redundancy. We contribute two novel strategies: Longevity-Aware Expanded Modulo Scheduling (LAEMS) with dependency relaxation, proactive reordering, and parallel expansion search, and Front-Back Block Fusion (FBBF) for cross-boundary scheduling. Evaluation on 13 benchmarks across two production VLIW-SIMD processors demonstrates LASM achieves 103.6% and 101.6% of expert assembly performance while reducing manual code by 72.6%. A full YOLOv5 deployment validates production applicability at 95.9% of expert performance. Code is available at https://github.com/urays/lasm.</jats:p>

title: PolarGate: Breaking the Functionality Representation Bottleneck of And-Inverter Graph Neural Network
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
0aa9885c6dd1a82ee1b521ebf2ec7bff9bf19fb8.abstract: <jats:p>Understanding the functionality of Boolean networks is crucial for processes such as functional equivalence checking, logic synthesis, and malicious logic identification. With the proliferation of deep learning in electronic design automation (EDA), graph neural networks (GNNs) are widely used to embed and-inverter graphs (AIGs)—a standard form of Boolean networks—into vectorized representations. A key challenge in applying GNNs for Boolean representation is that although GNNs can effectively encapsulate the structural properties of AIGs, they struggle to efficiently capture Boolean logic functionality. In this work, we focus on breaking this bottleneck by enhancing the functional representation capability of GNNs, proposing PolarGate, an efficient solution that not only aligns message passing with AIG logical functionality but also effectively integrates global information. Leveraging the intrinsic ambipolar states (0 and 1) of AIG nodes, PolarGate maps gate behavior into an ambipolar state space, customizes differentiable logical operators, and designs a functionality-aware message passing strategy. To further capture global circuit information, PolarGate integrates a structure-aware preprocessing module and a global linear attention module, transcending the locality constraint of message passing. Experimental results on two functionality-related basic tasks (signal probability prediction and truth-table distance prediction) and a downstream task (logic equivalence prediction) show that PolarGate outperform state-of-the-art GNN-based methods.</jats:p>

title: ODCGate: Leveraging Observability Don’t Care Conditions for Enhanced Power Efficiency in Clock Gating
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
9cab47548290de0fcb0e5c4f5470bbe3c4f9a5e9.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Clock gating reduces dynamic power by integrating activation functions and integrated clock gating (ICG) cells into the clock path, selectively disabling the clock signal to register when unnecessary. While conventional activation function extraction methods rely on manual design or register-transfer level analysis, a gate-level alternative exists: deriving activation functions through the extraction of observability don’t care (ODC) conditions from the underlying netlist. This article presents
                    <jats:bold>ODCGate</jats:bold>
                    , a framework designed to automatically detect ODC conditions as the activation functions and safely block clock transitions for unused registers, thereby further reducing dynamic power consumption during clock gating. The computation begins with cut boundary enumeration and simulation. To further minimize additional PPA overhead, we apply hybrid simplification techniques to the extracted logic, and enable sharing among registers through clustering. Experimental results show that, beyond the clock gating optimization of a commercial logic synthesis tool, our method achieves an average 33.46% additional reduction in dynamic power, with minimal impact on other PPA metrics.
                  </jats:p>

title: EnVector: Encoding using Pattern based Vectors for Energy Efficient Non-Volatile Main Memories
container-title: ACM Transactions on Design Automation of Electronic Systems
5243326e813a5b6c6c744dd3b22a5532319d4f01.abstract:
<jats:p>
                    Non-Volatile Memories (NVMs) provide new opportunities for scalable main memory due to their great scalability and other favorable attributes. However, considering their inherent write defects (long latency, high energy consumption), combined with their limited write endurance, their inclusion into the memory hierarchy requires careful handling. This not only shortens the lifespan of NVMs but also renders them as an expensive option. In this work, we propose a technique called
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">EnVector</jats:italic>
                    that exploits the intrinsic uniformity in memory data to encode the cacheline data before the memory write takes place. By using well-designed fixed vectors, it minimizes the variation between the incoming and the stored data. This saves a lot of possible bit flips, reducing the likelihood of any memory failure from an excessive number of writes. Consequently, improving performance and lowering latency and energy requirements. We empirically demonstrated that
                    <jats:italic toggle="yes">EnVector</jats:italic>
                    upgrades the NVM lifetime by 37% and accelerates its performance by 15% over the baseline.
                  </jats:p>
                  <jats:p/>

title: Design and Implementation of a Vision Integrated Autonomous Research Rover
2e019a77a34534cace9acae8857fa40918f60895.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents the design and implementation of a low-cost, vision-integrated autonomous rover for automated soil data collection. Traditional soil sampling methods are labor-intensive, and existing robotic solutions frequently depend on costly hardware and Global Positioning System (GPS) navigation, which can easily degrade in obstructed environments. To address these issues, a GPS-denied rover was developed using a Raspberry Pi 4B for high-level computer vision and a Robot Operating System 2 (ROS2) framework, paired with an Arduino Nano for real-time hardware control. The platform utilizes a linear actuator to autonomously deploy sensing probes for localized soil analysis. For stable navigation, an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) is implemented to fuse wheel encoder odometry with inertial data. An OpenCV-based vision pipeline directs autonomous path following and marker detection. To mitigate tracking errors caused by processing and mechanical latency, a custom delay-compensation filter is introduced to actively reverse the rover and correct overshoot. This is paired with a history-dependent sweep prioritization algorithm that intelligently re-acquires lost paths based on prior trajectory data. The resulting system provides a reliable, accessible framework for independent environmental monitoring.</jats:p>

title: MLLM-Driven Autonomous Driving: Closed-Loop Decision-Making with Language-State Alignment and Human Instruction Integration
container-title: ACM Journal on Autonomous Transportation Systems
d800c7e114eb4db4826982c6e016151dc7d88ec1.abstract: <jats:p>The core challenge of autonomous driving is achieving real-time decision-making and safety control in complex, dynamic environments, especially in long-tail scenarios where conventional systems often fail due to limited adaptability, poor human-vehicle interaction, and low interpretability. This article introduces MLLM-CLAD, a closed-loop decision-making framework powered by a multimodal large language model, which addresses semantic gaps and feedback limitations through a co-optimization strategy that integrates behavior-state alignment and language instruction fusion. MLLM-CLAD integrates three core modules: (1) The Mapping-Enhanced Language-State Alignment Module employs a deterministic mapping pipeline from language instructions to control signals, which enables highly accurate mapping from LLM semantic outputs to executable control signals. (2) The Hierarchical Dynamic Instruction Integration Module robustly categorizes and dynamically prioritizes human language instructions into different semantic types. (3) The Multimodal Fusion Module leverages a lightweight spatiotemporal Q-Former to jointly encode images and LiDAR point clouds, aligned with language in latent space for improved temporal reasoning and cross-modal consistency. Evaluated in the CARLA Town05 Long, MLLM-CLAD achieves a 78.3% Driving Score and reduces collision rates by 35% in safety-critical scenarios. On the LangAuto benchmarks, MLLM-CLAD attains a 78.5% long-tail scenario pass rate. Furthermore, the end-to-end latency is reduced to 128 milliseconds. This work establishes a scalable path toward safe, low-latency, and interpretable autonomous driving in simulation, with a clear roadmap for real-world extension.</jats:p>

title: Study Design and Lessons Learned From Using Google Takeout Donations for Suicide Prevention Research: Prospective Cohort Study
container-title: Journal of Medical Internet Research
6610fc8dba7dec763399be61f0e967f4f50c2399.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:sec sec-type="background">
                    <jats:title>Background</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Social media and search engine tech companies, such as Google, use the wealth of data at their disposal to create algorithms to predict suicide risk and provide interventions based on company policies and outputs from these algorithms. Neither the details of these algorithms nor their accuracy in risk prediction are shared with the public; thus, research is needed to verify whether algorithms applied to search engine data can accurately predict suicide risk in a platform user.
